title: Decoupling Framework and Composition Engineering via Sequential Selenium Source Switching for Efficient Sb2(S,Se)3 Thin Film Solar Cells
content:
A selenium‐source‐switching two‐step sequential deposition (SDE) strategy is developed for Sb2(S,Se)3 absorbers. It decouples framework construction and compositional tuning to trigger bulk ion diffusion and recrystallization, optimizing vertical Se/S grading and suppressing bulk and surface traps. The fabricated device delivers 10.90% efficiency, offering a universal route for high‐quality chalcogenide films.








ABSTRACT
Antimony selenosulfide (Sb2(S,Se)3) has recently attracted intense interest as an earth‐abundant, non‐toxic, and bandgap‐tunable photovoltaic absorber. However, conventional one‐step deposition routes typically produce films with inadequate crystallinity and inhomogeneous elemental distribution through the film thickness, which severely hamper charge transport and limit device performance. Herein, we introduce an innovative selenium‐source switching driven two‐step sequential deposition (SDE) strategy that decouples framework formation from compositional engineering to overcome these limitations. First, a selenourea‐based precursor is used to deposit a thick Sb2(S,Se)3 film serving as a primary light‐harvesting scaffold. Then, a sodium selenosulfate‐based precursor solution is applied for secondary deposition. Owing to the high reactivity of this solution system, selenium species readily penetrate into the as‐deposited film, inducing extensive ion diffusion and recrystallization throughout the bulk Sb2(S,Se)3 material. This SDE strategy simultaneously optimizes the vertical Se/S grading, tailors the bandgap profile, and eliminates bulk deep‐level traps and surface recombination centers. Consequently, the SDE‐Sb2(S,Se)3 device achieves a remarkable efficiency of 10.90%, placing it among the highest efficiencies for this material system. This strategy not only resolves the intrinsic bottlenecks of one‐step techniques but also provides a generalizable route for synthesizing high‐quality multicomponent chalcogenide films and offers new insights into ion‐exchange kinetics during sequential deposition.
journal: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents

title:
Carbon Insertion into
Electron-Deficient (Aza)indoles
via a Radical-Polar Crossover Strategy
content:
Abstract
Despite a surge of progress in both strategic approaches and reagent design, carbon insertion into indoles remains limited to electron-rich substrates, notwithstanding the prevalence of electron-poor (aza)indoles in medicinal chemistry. We report herein a radical-polar crossover strategy that overcomes this limitation through a photocatalytic, iodomethyl-radical-mediated cyclopropanation/autoxidation approach. The method enables access to a range of highly substituted, electron-poor quinolines, naphthyridines, and triazanaphthalenes, many of which are challenging to prepare by traditional syntheses. We demonstrate the modification of medicinally relevant (aza)indoles, and preliminary mechanistic observations support autoxidation via an anionic cyclopropane ring opening pathway.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
Scalable
Fluorinated Copper-Based Covalent Organic
Frameworks for Coupled Ultratrace Perfluoroalkyl Substances Monitoring
and Efficient Remediation
content:
Abstract
Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent water contaminants that require both effective removal and reliable monitoring. However, these functions are typically performed separately, preventing real-time evaluation of treatment performance. Here we establish a cooperative host–guest-coupling principle, in which a single host–guest binding event simultaneously drives contaminant capture and modulates the Cu-centered redox process, thereby generating concentration-dependent electrochemical signals within a porous framework. Guided by this principle, we reported a scalable fluorinated copper-based covalent organic framework (F–Cu–COF) synthesized through an open-air one-pot strategy that enables gram-scale production while retaining high crystallinity and chemical stability. Fluorinated pore domains and redox-active Cu centers create a cooperative host–guest environment that promotes PFAS binding and enrichment with electrochemical signal generation. Consequently, F–Cu–COF achieves a detection limit of 5.2 pg L–1, an uptake capacity of 3824 mg g–1, and efficient flow-through removal. This work establishes host–guest coupling as a common molecular basis for linking electrochemical signal generation with contaminant capture in scalable porous materials, providing a general design strategy for multifunctional water-treatment platforms capable of integrated treatment verification.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
Interhalogen of Iodine
Chloride Accelerates Charge
Transfer for Efficient Li 2 O 2  Oxidation in Lithium–Oxygen
Batteries
content:
Abstract
Li–O2 batteries suffer from sluggish Li2O2 oxidation kinetics at electrode/electrolyte interfaces, leading to large charge polarization and low energy efficiency. Soluble redox mediators (RMs) provide a solution-mediated pathway for Li2O2 decomposition and reduce the charge overpotential. However, the chemical oxidation of Li2O2 by oxidized RMs remains kinetically sluggish, resulting in persistent charge polarization. Herein, iodine monochloride (ICl), an interhalogen compound, is electrochemically generated in situ during the charge process to promote the oxidation of Li2O2. The large electronegativity difference between I and Cl promotes intramolecular charge transfer from I to Cl, creating an electrophilic iodine center (Iδ+) that increases the I–Cl bond polarity and strengthens the interaction with Li2O2. This lowers the decomposition barrier of Li2O2 from 2.39 to 0.77 eV, thereby facilitating its chemical oxidation. The Li–O2 battery delivers a low discharge/charge polarization of 0.52 V, effectively mitigating parasitic reactions at high voltages and enabling an extended cycling lifespan exceeding 800 h. This work provides a valuable design principle for developing redox mediators for efficient Li2O2 oxidation.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
Support Protection
Mechanism Enables Efficient and
Stable Anion Exchange Membrane Water Electrolyzers
content:
Abstract
Designing oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalysts that simultaneously achieve high activity and long-term stability remains a critical challenge for the development of alkaline anion exchange membrane water electrolyzers (AEMWEs). Here, we uncover a unique support protection mechanism in which lattice-confined ruthenium (Ru) single atoms offer robust protection for the spinel Co3O4 support, realizing outstanding stability in AEMWEs. Theoretical calculations and structural characterizations reveal that lattice confinement promotes the formation of robust Ru–O–Co bridges by simultaneously shortening the Co–O and Ru–O bond lengths, thereby suppressing Co dissolution and optimizing the electronic structure for efficient catalysis. Furthermore, in situ electrochemical analysis demonstrates that the lattice confinement of Ru atoms accelerates OER kinetics through facilitated proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) steps and partially activated lattice oxygen. As a result, the RuLCA-Co3O4 dominated by the adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) exhibits a lower overpotential of 260 mV at 10 mA cm–2, which is lower than that of RuSCA-Co3O4 dominated by the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM) pathway. Meanwhile, the lattice-confined RuLCA-Co3O4 exhibits nearly 9-fold lower Co dissolution compared to surface-coordinated RuSCA-Co3O4 after an accelerated durability test (ADT). Moreover, RuLCA-Co3O4 maintains an outstanding stability for over 1000 h in an AEMWE system with a low degradation rate of 88.1 μV h–1, outperforming RuSCA-Co3O4. This work establishes lattice confinement as an effective strategy to decouple activity-stability trade-offs in alkaline OER and provides a viable design principle for durable AEMWE anodes.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
Decoupling Dissolution
from Water Oxidation at Single-Faceted
High-Entropy Perovskite Electrodes
content:
Abstract
High-entropy oxides (HEOs) are promising anode materials for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) due to their wide compositional space and electronic flexibility. However, their electrochemical dissolution and OER remain concurrent, preventing decoupled analysis of dissolution kinetics and stability. Here, we present a combined atomic force microscopy (AFM) and scanning electrochemical cell microscopy (SECCM) strategy to decouple lattice dissolution from water oxidation under well-defined reaction conditions. Structurally analogous, atomically flat, single-faceted (001) ABO3 perovskite electrodes, La1–xSrx(Cr0.2Mn0.2Fe0.2Co0.2Ni0.2)O3 with x = 0 and 0.3, serve as model systems to probe dissolution and OER kinetics in acid. Pipet-probed localized cyclic voltammetry and chronoamperometry reveal that the measured current contains contributions from both OER and lattice dissolution, the latter producing nanoscale dissolution pits beneath the SECCM droplet. By correlating pit-growth kinetics with total OER charge as a function of pulse duration (τ), overpotential (η), and pH, we quantitatively separate dissolution from OER. The proportional scaling between dissolution charge and total charge indicates that OER and dissolution proceed within a common kinetic regime, sharing a common intermediate. A rate-law-based analysis yields the standard dissolution rate constant (kd0 cm/s), transfer coefficient (α), and proton reaction order (b) for the dissolution of the 001 facet of both HEO-P. Our results unravel how aliovalent A-site substitution (30% Sr2+) alters dissolution kinetics, charge partitioning between dissolution and OER, and thickness-dependent stability, thereby enabling quantitative disentangling of the intrinsic activity and stability of HEO electrodes.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
A Pseudo-Icosahedral
RhH 2 Au 10  Superatom: Two Hydrogen Atoms Acting
as Gold-Atom Equivalents and
Modifiers
content:
Abstract
A hydrogen atom is known to act as a gold-atom-equivalent dopant in gold nanoclusters (AuNCs) by contributing to the valence electron count. To gain insights into the interaction of multiple H atoms with AuNCs, we herein synthesized a di-H-atom-doped NC, [RhH2Au10(dppp)5]3+ (RhH2Au10; dppp = 1,3-bis(diphenylphosphino)propane), by exposing [RhAu10(dppp)5]3+ (RhAu10) to H2 gas; RhAu10 was generated in situ via hydride (H–) abstraction from [RhHAu10(dppp)5]2+. Comprehensive characterization of RhH2Au10 by X-ray crystallography, NMR spectroscopy, and theoretical calculations revealed that the two H atoms occupy the two “missing” Au sites in the arachno-type RhAu10 core via dissociative adsorption of H2, forming a pseudo-icosahedral RhH2Au10 core. This core structure contrasts sharply with the previously reported di-H-atom-doped silver- or copper-based superatoms, in which the H atoms form an MH2 (M = Os, Ru, Rh) unit completely encapsulated within an icosahedral Ag12 or Cu12 shell. The RhH2Au10 core possesses an 8-electron closed-shell electronic configuration of (1S)2(1P)6, which is isoelectronic to the icosahedral RhAu12 superatom, thereby demonstrating the Au-atom equivalence of H atoms. Nevertheless, the two H atoms in the RhH2Au10 superatomic core act as structural modifiers compared to the RhAu12 superatom: (1) the degeneracy of the 1P orbitals is lifted by lowering the geometric symmetry, and (2) the HOMO–LUMO energy gap is expanded due to the reduced electronic confinement volume. This study demonstrates that multiple H atoms in a gold-based superatomic core not only behave as Au-atom equivalents but also serve as key components for modulating their fundamental properties.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
Enhancing Propanol
Production from CO 2  Reduction
with a Terbium-Doped Copper Nitride Electrocatalyst
content:
Abstract
Propanol is one of the most complex products obtained from CO2 electroreduction (CO2R). Being an interesting precursor for synthetic fuels and a feedstock for the chemical industry, its electrochemical production has recently raised increasing interest. However, low selectivity for propanol has been achieved so far. Here, via exploring a variety of original lanthanide-doped copper nitride materials, we identified and characterized terbium-doped copper nitride as the most selective catalyst for propanol formation. It allowed CO2R to yield propanol with a Faradaic efficiency of 27% at a high current density of 300 mA cm–2 within a neutral (KHCO3 electrolyte) flow cell, surpassing the performance of previous CO2R catalysts. The high density of undercoordinated nitride-derived Cu sites, combined with the increased oxophilicity of the surface, likely promoted the selectivity toward alcohols. Thorough DFT calculations showed that Tb doping increased the affinity for oxygenate-associated C2* intermediates and lowered the free-energy barrier for reactions coupling the latter with CO* toward propanol.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
Layer-Distortion Engineering
of Acridinium-Based Covalent
Organic Frameworks Enables Efficient Photoredox Transformations of
Alcohols
content:
Abstract
Planar two-dimensional (2D) covalent organic frameworks (COFs) often suffer from severe interlayer π–π stacking, which promotes excitonic recombination, restricts access to active sites, and compromises photocatalytic efficiency. Here we report a layer-distortion engineering strategy to construct wavy acridinium-based COFs, Mes-Acr-TAPB and Mes-Acr-TAPP, by introducing structural distortion into otherwise planar layered frameworks. The resulting wavy framework efficiently suppresses interlayer π–π stacking, enlarges interlayer spacing, modulates molecular packing, pore environment, and improves accessibility to photoactive acridinium sites. Compared with the planar analog Dur-Acr-TAPB, Mes-Acr-TAPB exhibits enhanced exciton dissociation along with substrate absorption, more efficient charge separation, and superior photocatalytic activity. As a heterogeneous photoredox catalyst, Mes-Acr-TAPB enables diverse alcohol transformations under mild conditions, including β-scission radical functionalization, ring contraction/expansion, and skeletal transposition. Mes-Acr-TAPB shows broad functional-group tolerance and supports late-stage structural modification of complex natural products, highlighting its synthetic utility. This work establishes layer-distortion as an effective design principle for mitigating interlayer stacking in 2D COFs and advancing high-performance COF photocatalysts for sustainable organic synthesis.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
Kinetic Control of
Polymorphism in Li 10.5 Si 1.5 P 1.5 S 12 –Based Solid
Electrolytes
content:
Abstract
Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS)-type solid electrolytes (SEs) are among the most promising materials for next-generation solid-state batteries (SSBs) due to their high lithium-ion conductivity. However, challenges related to phase stability and polymorphism, especially in Ge-free, Si-based systems, limit their practical implementation. Here, the crystallization and phase transition behavior of materials with a nominal composition of Li10.5–xSi1.5P1.5S12–xIx (x = 0, 0.2, 0.4) are systematically investigated. Operando high-temperature synchrotron X-ray diffraction, total scattering with pair distribution function analysis, and differential scanning calorimetry measurements reveal the formation of a metastable orthorhombic (o) phase, followed by transformation into the thermodynamically stable tetragonal (t) phase at elevated temperatures. Our findings indicate that lithium iodide (LiI) as an additive regulates the crystallization of the o-phase and thereby governs the transition kinetics. This enables the o-to-t phase transition to occur at much reduced temperatures and faster rates. Neutron powder diffraction further uncovers minor modifications to the Si/P ratio and lithium sublattice, as well as the fact that iodine is not incorporated into the t-phase; instead, a secondary Li4PS4I-type phase forms. Collectively, this work highlights the critical role of microstructural engineering on crystallization and polymorphism in LGPS-type SEs and also demonstrates the applicability of these dual-phase materials by enabling high-performance lithium–sulfur SSBs.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
Efficient Chemical
Synthesis and Enzymatic Replication
of 3′-Deoxyapionucleic Acid (ApioNA): An RNA-Selective XNA
with Conformational Flexibility
content:
Abstract
Xeno-nucleic acids (XNAs) have emerged as versatile platforms due to their sugar scaffolds that enable precise chemical tuning, leading to distinct classes ranging from fully compatible systems to orthogonal systems. However, sugar-modified XNAs capable of discriminating between RNA and DNA have remained elusive. In this work, we establish 3′-deoxyapionucleic acid (ApioNA) as a structurally flexible XNA with inherent RNA-selective hybridization properties. We achieved efficient production of ApioNA oligonucleotides through an efficient asymmetric synthesis of their building blocks and systematically characterized their properties. Thermal melting analyses demonstrate that ApioNA forms moderately stable duplexes with RNA while exhibiting weak pairing with DNA and negligible self-association. Quantum mechanical calculations reveal that the apiofuranose ring populates two low-energy puckering states, and the addition of an extra methylene group enhances backbone flexibility, thereby favoring A-form geometry for RNA pairing while requiring a higher-energy state to accommodate B-form DNA. Despite its weak affinity for DNA, ApioNA supports a complete enzymatic replication cycle using commercial Therminator and Bst 3.0 polymerases with approximately 98% fidelity and is processed by native E. coli machinery in vivo. This work fills the RNA-selective niche in the XNA functional landscape and establishes sugar puckering dynamics and backbone flexibility as key design principles for programming nucleic acid pairing specificity.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
Boosting Ionomer Oxygen
Transport via Pore Confinement
in Carbon Supports for Low-Pt Fuel Cells
content:
Abstract
Low-Pt proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) are promising for hydrogen energy implementation, yet oxygen transport through ionomer-covered catalyst surfaces becomes increasingly limiting due to the resistance associated with dense ionomer films. Herein, we demonstrate a pore-confinement strategy to manipulate the spatial locality of Pt nanoparticles within porous carbon supports, enabling simultaneous regulation of ionomer distribution and molecular organization. Pt nanoparticles were selectively positioned on the external surfaces (Ptext/PC) or within the internal nanopores (Ptint/PC) of otherwise comparable supports, while maintaining similar Pt loading, particle size, and pore characteristics. Under H2-air condition, Ptint/PC delivered a peak power density ∼1.3 times higher than that of Ptext/PC, but a similar current density in the high-voltage region. Electrochemical analyses reveal that the performance enhancement originates from improved oxygen transport rather than catalytic activity. Wide-angle X-ray scattering and molecular dynamics simulations reveal that the Pt nanoparticles confined within mesopores disrupt the dense packing of ionomer backbones, thereby boosting oxygen permeability at the catalyst–ionomer interface. By establishing a direct relationship between Pt locality, ionomer distribution, backbone organization, and oxygen transport, this work identifies catalyst locality as an effective parameter for engineering interfacial mass transport and provides a new design principle for low-Pt PEMFCs.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
Electrochemical Synthesis
of Slaked Lime Utilizing
a Diaphragm Flow Cell
content:
Abstract
Slaked lime (Ca(OH)2) is one of the most widely utilized chemicals, with applications in diverse industries including construction, mining, water treatment, and chemical manufacturing. Currently, Ca(OH)2 is synthesized by coal-fired calcination of CaCO3 to make CaO, followed by exothermic hydration. Converting CaCO3 into Ca(OH)2 using electrochemically generated acid and base has attracted great interest because it could be powered by renewable electricity and would generate the CO2 byproduct in a pure form. Previous electrochemical Ca(OH)2 syntheses have incorporated the processing of calcium salts within the electrochemical cell to avoid acid–base recombination losses, but these cells have poor stability and high energy demand. Herein, we show that production of high-salinity acid and base solutions using a diaphragm flow cell (DFC) coupled with ex situ processing of CaCO3 substantially improves the efficiency of electrochemical Ca(OH)2 production. Using a closed loop with a simple KCl salt solution, we demonstrate the synthesis of >99% pure Ca(OH)2 for 0.088 to 0.10 kWh per mole at productive current densities of 158 to 334 mA cm–2.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
Synthetic
W/Cu Mimics of the Mo/Cu Active Site in
Aerobic CODH: Nonclassical Isocyanide Coordination and the Role of
the Bridging Sulfide
content:
Abstract
Aerobic carbon monoxide dehydrogenase (CODH) uses an unsupported Mo–S–Cu heterobimetallic active site to catalyze CO oxidation, but the mechanistic role of the bridging sulfide remains to be fully resolved. We report a series of W/Cu complexes designed to test whether steric shielding from a bidentate tBuxantphos ligand can suppress unwanted Cu···Sdithiolate and Cu···O═M interactions that plagued the reactivity of a previously reported NHC-ligated model system. Addition of [Cu(tBuxantphos)]+ to [(bdt)WVI(O)(OSiiPr3)(X)]− (bdt = 1,2-benzenedithiolate; X = O, S, Se) unexpectedly favors Cu coordination at the W═O rather than the W═X unit, giving X═W–O–Cu cores as the thermodynamically preferred isomers, opposite to the connectivity predicted by hard–soft acid–base theory and found in CODH itself. The resulting complexes bind isocyanides at CuI with nonclassical (blue-shifted) C≡N stretching frequencies. In contrast, no reactivity is observed toward CO gas, consistent with DFT predictions that CO coordination is endergonic. However, the calculations reveal that the CO adduct of the hypothetical O═W–S–Cu–CO isomer is more stabilized than its S═W–O–Cu–CO counterpart, an effect traced by molecular orbital analysis to delocalization of electron density from the redox-active dithiolate through the bridging sulfide into the Cu–CO π-backbonding manifold. These results provide an electronic rather than purely structural rationale for why the CODH active site retains a bridging sulfide despite an apparent thermodynamic preference for a bridging oxo in the synthetic analogues investigated here.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
Intricate Proteoform
Heterogeneity in the Tailpiece
of IgA within and across Its Circulatory and Secretory Configurations
content:
Abstract
Human immunoglobulin A (IgA) naturally occurs in multiple molecular forms─monomers, dimers, and even higher-order polymers─that are differentially distributed across serum, breast milk, and mucosal surfaces. The C-terminal tailpiece of IgA is essential to its polymerization mediated by the joining chain (J-chain) and thus also an important determinant of its extensive structural heterogeneity, yet its features remain somewhat poorly defined. Here, we used HILIC-LC-MS/MS-based glycopeptide analysis to characterize the N-glycan structures, disulfide linkages, and C-terminal amino acid sequence variants within the IgA tailpiece across the different molecular configurations of endogenous IgA. We find extensive correlation between these post-translational modifications; i.e., variations in tailpiece Asn459 N-glycosylation, redox status and disulfide connectivity of Cys471, and the presence or absence of C-terminal Tyr472 are intrinsically interconnected. When Cys471 was disulfide-bound to the J-chain, Asn459 glycans showed broader structural heterogeneity and retained more high-mannose structures, whereas free Cys471 tailpieces mainly carried mature, sialylated complex-type glycans. Serum IgA and milk SIgA displayed distinct tailpiece signatures, including differences in N-glycan maturation and processing of the ultimate C-terminal Tyr472 residue. Together, these findings define biofluid-specific molecular forms of IgA and highlight the remarkable structural diversity of the human IgA tailpiece. Overall, our results advance the understanding of the IgA structure and could offer a much-needed molecular basis to assist future bioengineering of IgA-based therapeutics.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
A Microporous Zr-Tetraphosphonate
MOF with Permanent
Porosity, Robustness, and Thermochemical Heat Storage Capability
content:
Abstract
Combining high-valent metal cations with phosphonate linkers represents a promising strategy to address the limited stability of MOFs, yet permanently porous phosphonate MOFs (P-MOFs) remain rare due to the strong coordination propensity of phosphonate groups. Herein, we report IEF-10, a new microporous zirconium tetraphosphonate framework constructed from ZrO5F octahedral secondary building units and a pyrene tetraphosphonate linker. The material combines three features that are seldom achieved simultaneously in P-MOFs: permanent accessible microporosity (equivalent BET surface area ∼430 m2·g–1), accessible phosphonic acid functionalities (-PO3H), and exceptional thermal (up to 450 °C), mechanical (>3 tons), and chemical stability (pH 1–12, organic solvents). The structure exhibits reversible water adsorption with moderate uptake and experimentally determined capacities of heat storage of ∼400–500 J·g–1, reflecting a favorable balance between host–guest interactions and regeneration requirements. As a proof of concept, IEF-10 was evaluated for thermochemical heat storage under dynamic moist-gas flow conditions. Calorimetric measurements revealed fast heat-release kinetics (3–4 h), and excellent cyclability in terms of heat release (at least 10 cycles, total test duration of 5 weeks). The hydrophobic surface character is an advantage for long-term storage uses as the adsorbent can remain in a dry state between the charging and discharging stages even at low relative humidity levels in the reactor. These results demonstrate how the combination of permanent porosity, accessible phosphonic acid groups, and exceptional framework robustness can enable functional adsorption-driven energy storage while providing new opportunities for the development of porous zirconium P-MOFs.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
Fluorine-Mediated Molten-Salt
Crystallization Regulates
Phase Evolution and Structural Stability in Sodium Layered Oxides
content:
Abstract
Ni- and Co-free P2-type Fe–Mn layered oxides with high Na concentrations are promising cathodes for sodium-ion batteries, but their practical use is limited by phase instability during Na-excess synthesis and structural degradation during cycling and storage. Although large single-crystal-like architectures could improve stability, controlled phase-selective crystallization in these cathode systems remains challenging. Here, we show that fluorine-assisted molten-salt synthesis enables controlled formation of large-particle Fe–Mn–Ti P2 cathodes with enhanced phase selectivity and structural coherence. Compared with Na-excess processing alone, NaF-assisted flux growth expands the P2 phase stability window and promotes large particles with uniform morphologies while preserving local layered ordering. Multiscale characterization further reveals more-reversible structural evolution and more homogeneous Mn redox behavior in the NaF-assisted material, together with a gradient-like fluorine distribution involving surface-enriched NaF-like species and lower level interior fluorine environments. These coupled structural, morphological, and chemical features collectively mitigate crack formation and deliver good cycling stability. In summary, NaF-assisted molten-salt synthesis shows promise in addressing key limitations of Ni- and Co-free P2-type Fe–Mn layered cathodes.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
G-Quadruplex-Interacting
Photooxidative Platinum(IV)
Prodrug for Inhibiting Oncogene Transcription and Amplifying Antitumor
Immunity
content:
Abstract
Conventional platinum (Pt)-based chemotherapeutics elicit cancer cell death primarily through DNA binding, but this approach is inherently limited by poor site specificity and a lack of spatiotemporal control, which compromises therapeutic precision and safety. To overcome these limitations, we report DNATplatin, an in situ activatable and photooxidative Pt(IV) prodrug designed to combine precise recognition of DNA secondary structures with targeted genetic intervention through DNA photooxidation. By incorporating a bis-N-methylpyridinium moiety to selectively recognize DNA, DNATplatin shows a 10-fold increase in the levels in genomic DNA relative to oxaliplatin and a 2.5-fold emission turn-on selectivity for G-quadruplexes (G4s) over typical duplex DNA. Following precise nuclear localization, photoactivated DNATplatin acts as a potent photooxidant that oxidizes G4, dismantles G4 scaffolds, and abrogates circular dichroism signatures. These orchestrated lesions generate localized oxidative stress and selectively silence major G4-driven oncogenes, thereby effectively circumventing traditional Pt resistance by bypassing canonical adduct-dependent pathways. In a murine triple-negative breast tumor model, DNATplatin produces profound tumor suppression and elicits a robust systemic immune response, characterized by CD4+/CD8+ T-cell activation and depletion of Foxp3+ regulatory T cells. Collectively, this work establishes a controllable “target-and-destroy” strategy and underscores the potential of Pt(IV) photooxidants for topology-selective genetic intervention.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
Sugar-Based 1-Dimensional
Metal–Organic
Chalcogenolates with Hydration-Tunable Chiroptical Emission
content:
Abstract
Chiral topology in semiconductors introduces a structural degree of freedom for tuning the chiroptical, excitonic, and spintronic behavior. In metal–organic chalcogenolates (MOChas) semiconductors, how ligand stereochemistry and supramolecular organization influence chiral topology, and thus optical and excitonic responses, remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate intrinsic circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) in sugar-based 1-dimensional MOChas, with structures solved via small-molecule serial femtosecond crystallography. These materials exhibit blue and green CPLs, arising from the chiral inorganic core. Despite the close chemical similarity between the glucose- and galactose-derived ligands, we observed dramatic differences in their inorganic structure. Silver glucosethiolate shows reversible hydration-driven photoluminescence switching with a hydration-linked emission energy. Labile water molecules in the glucose-based system correlate with a blueshift in excitonic emission. Our results suggest a new direction in the search for chirophotonic hybrid semiconductors, exploiting intrinsically chiral topologies and excitonic optical frequencies, which are sensitively modulated by ligand identity and supramolecular interactions.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
Core–Shell Structures
Govern Through-Space
Interactions in Triblock Copolymers toward Deep-Red Clusteroluminescence
content:
Abstract
Green fluorescent protein (GFP) and its derivatives have transformed biological imaging, yet fluorophores that simultaneously combine biocompatibility, structural programmability, and intrinsic long-wavelength luminescence remain scarce. Here, we develop a controllable one-pot polymerization strategy to construct nonconjugated triblock copolymers that can self-assemble into core–shell clusters. By modulating the hydrophilic–hydrophobic balance of copolymer chains, the core-to-shell ratio, chain packing, and electronic through-space interactions within the clusters can be precisely regulated, enabling tunable clusteroluminescence (CL) that extends to the deep-red and near-infrared emission region. Ultrafast spectroscopy further uncovers the excited-state dynamics of these core–shell clusters and reveals how the coupled evolution of electronic states and structures governs CL generation. Moreover, the core–shell clusters enable in vivo angiography under two-photon excitation, highlighting their potential as biocompatible nanofluorophores. These findings establish core–shell engineering as a general design principle for efficient clusteroluminogens, deepen the mechanistic understanding of CL, and pave the way for next-generation nanofluorescence technologies.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
Modifier-Driven Proton
Conductivity in Hybrid Glasses
above 200 °C
content:
Abstract
Compositional tuning is a cornerstone of inorganic glass science, yet analogous strategies remain underdeveloped for emerging metal–organic hybrid glasses. We introduce phosphate modification of zinc imidazolate glass as a route to hybrid glasses with tunable network connectivity and proton-conductive functionality. Melt-quenching of ZIF-zni with benzimidazolium dihydrogen phosphate (BP) affords a series of cm-scale, transparent bulk glasses across a wide compositional range. Systematic characterization reveals that modification proceeds through ligand exchange at zinc centers, increasing the average coordination number from 4 to above 5 and progressively depolymerizing the imidazolate network. Despite macroscopic homogeneity, X-ray total scattering identifies a quasi-periodic ordering at ∼11 Å, and 1H NMR spin relaxation establishes nanoscale phase segregation between ZIF-derived and BP-rich domains of 2–70 nm. This heterogeneity underpins proton transport under anhydrous conditions; conductivities of 10–5–10–3 S cm–1 at 240 °C follow Vogel–Tammann–Fulcher dynamics, confirming that segmental motion couples to ion mobility. Infiltrating the glass into a porous PTFE scaffold yields a composite membrane that achieves 8.4 × 10–5 S cm–1 at 170 °C under humidification and sustains steam electrolysis with near-unity Faradaic efficiency. These results establish network-modified hybrid glasses as a scalable and designable platform for intermediate-temperature solid electrolytes.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
Crossover from Asymmetric
to Symmetric Electrowetting
Linked to Double-Layer Restructuring
content:
Abstract
Voltage-controlled wetting at solid–liquid interfaces is central to the performance of a range of electrochemical and microfluidic technologies, yet the molecular basis of polarity-dependent electrowetting remains unresolved. Classical electrocapillarity predicts a symmetric dependence of contact angle on applied potential, but experiments and simulations frequently exhibit pronounced asymmetry. Here, combining electrowetting measurements with atomistic simulations, we show that asymmetric wetting at aqueous carbon interfaces arises from the structure of the electrical double layer. By investigating aqueous KF and LiCl electrolytes at graphitic interfaces across lower concentration and water-in-salt regimes, we identify a crossover from strongly asymmetric electrowetting at lower concentration to a symmetric response at high concentration for KF, while LiCl retains a pronounced asymmetry. This transition is accompanied by corresponding changes in the solid–liquid interfacial tension, demonstrating that polarity-dependent wetting can arise from voltage-dependent molecular restructuring of the interfacial liquid, which modifies the interfacial thermodynamics, without invoking faradaic processes. We introduce interfacial connectivity, defined by the network of intermolecular interactions within the first adsorption layer, as a molecular descriptor linking double-layer structure to macroscopic wetting behavior. These results demonstrate that electrolyte-controlled electrowetting can recover the symmetric electrocapillary limit under appropriate conditions and establish a unified framework connecting double-layer structure, interfacial free energy, and voltage-dependent wetting.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
Energy Deposition Timescales
Controls Chemistry in
Pulsed Methane Plasmas
content:
Abstract
Nonoxidative methane conversion offers a promising route for the coproduction of hydrogen and value-added hydrocarbons without CO2 emissions. Among emerging approaches, pulsed plasmas can provide potential advantages by enabling high energy deposition, rapid quenching, and generation of active nonthermal species. This work systematically investigates how pulsed energy deposition from nanosecond-to-millisecond time scales (10 to 50 mJ/pulse) influences methane plasma characteristics (electron density and gas temperature), reaction mechanisms, conversion, and energy efficiency. Nanosecond discharges produced the highest overall C2 selectivity (>70%), with up to 20% for C2H4; in this regime, methane dissociation proceeded through both electron-impact and thermal dissociation, whereas longer pulses were predominantly thermal. Pulsed plasma conversion was similar to thermal arcs (∼377 kJ/mol CH4) and specific energy requirements to produce C2H2 and H2 were 15 kWh/kg and 40 kWh/kg, respectively, in 100 μs long discharges. The product distribution was largely determined by thermal processes involving dehydrogenation reactions (Kassel’s reaction scheme). High gas temperatures preferentially favored C2H2 formation over C2H4, and C2H4 selectivity decreased with increasing pulse width. Overall, these results demonstrate that pulse width and energy can be used to tailor hydrocarbon selectivity and can help design pulsed plasma systems for efficient production of value-added hydrocarbons and hydrogen.

title:
Sky-Blue Thermally
Activated Delayed Fluorescence
from a Zirconium(IV) Complex
content:
Abstract
Earth-abundant early transition-metal complexes with luminescent ligand-to-metal charge-transfer (LMCT) excited states remain an attractive yet underexplored alternative to widely used precious-metal emitters. A fundamental understanding of the molecular design principles governing the photophysical properties of LMCT emitters is critical to further developing cost-effective and sustainable photochemical applications using this compound class. Here, we report the synthesis of a novel bis(4,5-ditolylamido-9,9-dimethylxanthene)zirconium complex, Zr(TolXDA)2, that shows efficient photoluminescence due to thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) at room temperature. Steady-state and time-resolved spectroscopic studies at room temperature reveal highly efficient and long-lived emission in the sky-blue and green wavelength range for solid samples (λPL = 480 nm, ΦPL = 0.60, τPL = 4–14 μs) and THF solutions (λPL = 548 nm, ΦPL = 0.30, τPL = 8 μs) of Zr(TolXDA)2, respectively. Despite the relatively large singlet–triplet energy gap (ΔEST ≥ 0.26 eV), TADF emission in Zr(TolXDA)2 is unambiguously confirmed by temperature-dependent emission studies. This is likely facilitated by the high LMCT character of the S1 and T1 states, a consequence of strategic ligand design, which allows for rapid forward and reverse intersystem crossing. This hypothesis is supported by femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy, which confirms facile forward and reverse intersystem crossing in Zr(TolXDA)2 (τISC = 15 ± 5 ps, τrISC = 0.48 ± 0.39 μs), and TD-DFT calculations, which establish significant negative charge transfer to zirconium in the lowest energy excited states.

title:
Catalytic
Enzymatic Hydrolysis Lignin Hydroconversion
Targeting Sustainable Aviation Fuels: Solvent Effect
content:
Abstract
In this study, we investigated the effect of the solvent on the hydroconversion of enzymatic hydrolysis lignin (EHL) using a NiMoS catalyst supported on an alumina-zeolite extrudate. The lignin was characterized via standard complementary techniques (size exclusion chromatography (SEC), NMR, and elemental analyses), with its low solubility to be taken into account. A comparison of the solvents for the conversion of EHL indicated that a H-donor solvent such as tetralin was indeed more effective in recovering a liquid fraction than hydrocarbon- and alcohol-based solvents. Alcohol solvents such as ethanol, in mixture with heptane, and isobutanol resulted only in a slight improvement in liquefaction under these operating conditions. The main drawbacks of alcohol and tetralin solvents are their tendency to react during hydroconversion, which complicates the analysis of the liquid fractions, making it difficult to assess the catalytic impact. Notably, the use of heptane enabled the production of a fully deoxygenated liquid fraction from EHL, consisting of a mixture of cycloalkanes, alkanes, and aromatics. Even if it is obtained with quite low yield from raw EHL, this mixture is fully consistent with the composition of jet fuel in terms of chemical groups and could easily be used, probably after finishing treatments, in the formulation of sustainable aviation fuels (SAFs).

title:
Mode-Aware
Production Forecasting of Coalbed Methane
Wells via Unsupervised Parameter-Image Clustering and Similarity-Based
GAF Correction
content:
Abstract
Accurate and efficient production forecasting is critical for coalbed methane (CBM) well development and management. However, conventional engineering methods rely heavily on physical assumptions and parameter calibration, whereas direct data-driven models typically establish a global input–output mapping without explicitly distinguishing different production patterns or exploiting similarities among samples, thereby limiting their forecasting accuracy and generalizability. To address these limitations, this study proposes a structured forecasting framework integrating parameter-image representation, unsupervised clustering, lightweight classification, and similarity-based correction. Geological and development parameters are first converted into grayscale images, and spectral clustering combined with K-means++ is used to identify production-related modes. A MobileNetV2-based classifier is then trained to determine the mode category of new samples. Within the identified category, the most similar sample is retrieved, and its production sequences are encoded as Gramian Angular Field (GAF) images. Difference-image-guided posterior correction is further applied before reconstructing the corrected images into production time series. Results based on numerical simulation samples show that the proposed framework achieves high accuracy for both gas and water production forecasting, with R2 values of 0.99 and 0.99 for daily gas and daily water production, respectively. Compared with representative machine-learning and deep-learning models, the proposed method demonstrates superior accuracy and efficiency, indicating its potential for rapid CBM production forecasting.

title:
Integrated
Photovoltaic-Supercapacitor Systems: Structural
Architectures, Materials Innovations, and Emerging Multifunctional
Designs
content:
Abstract
Renewable energy technologies that simultaneously harvest and store energy are attracting increasing attention as next-generation power solutions for portable, wearable, and self-powered electronic systems. Among these technologies, monolithically integrated solar energy conversion and storage devices that combine solar cells (SCs) with supercapacitors into singular, encapsulated structures offer a promising pathway to address the intermittency of solar power while enabling compact and multifunctional energy platforms. This review systematically summarizes recent progress in monolithically integrated solar energy harvesting and storage systems, with particular emphasis on structural architectures, photovoltaic configurations, electrode/electrolyte engineering, and multifunctional device designs. The advantages and limitations of two-electrode, three-electrode, and shared-substrate configurations are critically compared in terms of internal resistance, power matching, fabrication complexity, mechanical flexibility, and overall energy conversion-storage efficiency. Recent advances in rigid, flexible, and fibrous integrated systems based on silicon, dye-sensitized, perovskite, organic, and quantum-dot solar cells are comprehensively discussed, alongside emerging developments in photorechargeable supercapacitors, electrochromic systems, and multifunctional photovoltaic–triboelectric hybrid devices. Particular attention is given to the roles of advanced materials, including graphene, carbon nanotubes, MXenes, conductive polymers, and other low-dimensional materials, in enhancing electrochemical performance, flexibility, and device stability. Current challenges associated with electrolyte compatibility, device mismatch, mechanical durability, long-term cycling stability, scalability, and performance standardization are further analyzed. Finally, future perspectives toward high-efficiency, mechanically robust, and commercially viable integrated energy systems for wearable electronics, smart textiles, and distributed energy applications are outlined.

title:
Stepwise
Generation of Hydrogen and Oxygen in Water
Electrolysis via an Iodine-Based Redox Reaction
content:
Abstract
Water electrolysis is a promising method for producing hydrogen using clean energy. However, in conventional reactions, hydrogen and oxygen are generated simultaneously, requiring a robust structural design to prevent gas mixing and limiting the flexibility of the system. In this work, we aimed to produce these two gases separately by introducing redox species so that the system would become more flexible. Because the reaction potential of the redox species should lie between the hydrogen and oxygen evolution reaction potentials, iodine redox species were selected. In the first step, in which the evolution of oxygen is restrained, iodide ions are added to the anolyte to undergo an oxidation reaction, producing iodate ions. At a potential of +1.54 V (vs RHE), the faradaic efficiencies for the production of iodate ions and hydrogen were 98 and 98%, respectively. In the second step, when hydrogen evolution is suppressed, iodate ions are added to the catholyte to undergo a reduction reaction, producing iodide ions. At the potentials of −0.16 and −0.065 V (vs RHE), the maximum faradaic efficiency to produce iodide ions was achieved. Thus, hydrogen and oxygen were successfully produced individually with high efficiencies.

title:
Thermal-Hydraulic-Mechanical-Damage-Coupled Investigation
of CH 4  Displacement by N 2  and CO 2  Injection in Low-Permeability Coal
content:
Abstract
Gas injection is an effective strategy for CBM recovery in low-permeability coal reservoirs. However, the coupled evolution of gas migration, coal deformation-damage behavior, and the relative contributions of replacement and sweeping mechanisms during different gas injection processes remain insufficiently understood. In this study, a THMD-coupled numerical model was developed and validated against experimental data to investigate methane displacement behavior in low-permeability coal under N2 and CO2 injection conditions with different injection pressures. To quantitatively distinguish the displacement mechanisms, the Replacement-Sweeping Consumption Ratio (RSCR) was proposed, defined as the ratio of the amount of injected gas consumed through competitive adsorption for CH4 replacement to that transported in the free-gas state for CH4 sweeping. The results indicate that both N2 and CO2 injection significantly enhance CH4 recovery compared with natural drainage. N2 and CO2 injection increased cumulative CH4 production by up to 113% and 97%, respectively, with N2 exhibiting higher recovery performance under identical injection conditions. The two displacement gases differ markedly in permeability evolution: N2 injection undergoes a stable-rapid decline-gradual recovery three-stage process and ultimately outperforms natural drainage, whereas CO2 injection yields a continuous permeability drop via strong adsorption-driven matrix swelling with scarce local damage. Mechanism analysis revealed that N2 displacement is dominated by rapid diffusion and sweeping effects, which continuously promote CH4 desorption and migration. By contrast, CO2 displacement is primarily controlled by competitive adsorption replacement. Accordingly, CO2 exhibited substantially higher RSCR values than N2, indicating a greater relative contribution of adsorption-induced replacement, whereas N2 relied more strongly on free-gas sweeping. The combined effects of slow migration and permeability deterioration fostered high-concentration CH4 accumulation zones, forming an inhibition mechanism of rapid replacement but slow migration. The findings provide mechanistic insights into gas selection and injection pressure optimization for enhanced methane recovery in low-permeability coal reservoirs.

title:
Life-Cycle
Environmental and Economic Assessment of
Photovoltaic and Grid-Powered Green Hydrogen Chains in Northwest China
content:
Abstract
This study conducts a cradle-to-gate life-cycle environmental and economic assessment of industrial-scale hydrogen production in the Yumen Oilfield, Northwest China. Eight scenarios are established by combining photovoltaic (PV) or grid electricity, alkaline water electrolysis (AWE) or proton exchange membrane electrolysis (PEM), and pipeline or tube-trailer transportation over 100 km. Global warming potential (GWP), acidification potential (AP), metal depletion (MD), water consumption, and the levelized cost of hydrogen (LCOH) are evaluated. The results show that the electricity source is the dominant factor affecting the environmental performance. Compared with grid-powered scenarios, PV-powered hydrogen reduces GWP by up to 91% and water consumption by approximately 87%, although it increases MD because of the material requirements of PV infrastructure and, particularly for PEM-based pathways, electrolyzer stack manufacturing. Contribution analysis reveals that hard coal dominates grid-related GWP and AP, whereas hydropower is the primary contributor to grid-related water consumption. In PV-powered scenarios, truck transportation contributes significantly to the GWP and AP, indicating that downstream compression and transportation should not be neglected in industrial hydrogen supply chains. An integrated environmental-economic assessment shows that PV-powered hydrogen achieves a better balance between carbon reduction and cost performance than grid-powered hydrogen. Under the specific carbon-price and slow, medium, and fast development assumptions, PV-powered hydrogen is projected to approach or enter the cost range of gray hydrogen by 2035.

title: Electrically Enabled Isothermal CeO 2  Thermochemical Water Splitting below 900 °C
content:
Abstract
Ceria-based thermochemical cycles offer a promising route to solar hydrogen, but require reduction above 1400 °C and large temperature swings. Here, building on electrically assisted CeO2 reduction, we demonstrate repeated isothermal CeO2-based water-splitting cycles at 700–900 °C and 0.5–2.0 V. Porous CeO2−YSZ bilayer pellets with different composition ratios undergo electrically assisted reduction and steam re-oxidation at the same temperature, producing O2 and H2 in separate steps without thermal cycling. The process reaches H2/O2 ratios up to 1.9, reproducible H2 productivity over 10 cycles, and H2 yields up to 49 ± 2 μmol gCeO2−1 cycle−1 after only 20 min of electrically assisted reduction. Extended-reduction experiments show that the best composition remains only ∼0.10 V below the applied bias on an equivalent thermodynamic-voltage basis. Reactor-scale projections based on gas utilization in an existing ceria reactor give a solar-to-H2 efficiency of 5.6% without assuming improvements to the CeO2−YSZ architecture.

title: Rational Ionomer Design Directs Hydrogenation Pathways and Reactant Accessibility in Electrochemical Nitrate Reduction
content:
Abstract
Ionomer engineering offers a powerful yet underexplored strategy for electrochemical nitrate reduction (NO3RR), since the polymer tailors the microenvironment at the catalyst surface. Here, we rationally design high-performance ionomers by applying fixed-charge sign and hydration as design criteria. Synthetic anion-exchange ionomers (AEIs) enhance NO3– accessibility, and the highest AEI hydration is accompanied by a shift in the dominant hydrogenation pathway toward a favorable *H-mediated regime. Time-dependent attenuated total reflection surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (ATR-SEIRAS) coupled with numerical simulation yields a 40.7-fold higher NO3– diffusion coefficient for the AEI than for Nafion. Potential-dependent in situ ATR-SEIRAS combined with kinetic isotope effect measurements and *H scavenging supports a pathway shift arising from a hydrated microenvironment enriched in free and weakly hydrogen-bonded water. The AEI-modified commercial Cu nanoparticle electrode reaches an NH3 yield rate of 13.8 mg h–1cm–2 and 98.0% Faradaic efficiency, positioning the fixed-charge sign and hydration as accessible design descriptors potentially transferable to other electrocatalytic reactions.

title: Cesium-Triiodide-Mediated Crystallization Regulation of Pure-Iodide Wide-Bandgap Perovskites Enables Perovskite-Silicon Tandem Solar Cells Exceeding 30% Efficiency
content:
Abstract
Pure-iodide wide-bandgap (WBG) perovskites (∼1.68 eV) featuring eliminated photoinduced halide segregation are compelling top-cell absorbers for perovskite-silicon tandem solar cells. However, their complex crystallization readily induces heterogeneous composition and structural defects, hindering performance improvements in the resulting devices. Here, we develop a cesium triiodide (CsI3)-mediated strategy to regulate intermediate-phase evolution of pure-iodide WBG perovskites. The CsI3-derived precursor chemistry reconstructs Pb-I coordination networks, suppresses premature organic-dominated intermediate nucleation, and promotes homogeneous phase conversion. The modulated crystallization pathway yields highly crystalline films with improved iodine uniformity and reduced non-radiative recombination losses. Consequently, single-junction solar cells achieve a stabilized power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 22.40%, which retains 95% of its initial efficiency after 1500 h of maximum power point tracking. More importantly, the associated perovskite-silicon solar cells deliver a stabilized PCE of 30.74% along with improved thermal stability, highlighting the great potential of pure-iodide WBG perovskites for efficient and durable tandem photovoltaics.

title: An Efficient Mo-Doped Fe 3 S 4  Co-Catalyst on TiO 2  for Enhanced Photocatalytic Hydrogen Production
content:
Abstract
The development of earth-abundant co-catalysts that enhance TiO2-driven hydrogen evolution remains crucial for sustainable photocatalytic H2 production. This work investigates Mo addition as a compositional strategy to tune the co-catalytic functionality of Fe3S4 for photocatalytic HER over TiO2. A series of x%Mo–Fe3S4 (x = 0, 1, 2, 5, and 7.5) materials was prepared and evaluated using both conventional solvothermal synthesis (18 h) and a microwave-assisted non-aqueous sol–gel route requiring 30 min. When combined with anatase TiO2 as a model photocatalyst at a fixed co-catalyst loading (5 wt %), Mo addition markedly improved the performance of the Fe3S4 co-catalyst. Structural, surface, and optical characterizations indicate that Mo addition modifies the sulfides, in parallel with the observed improvement in co-catalytic hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) performance. Under UV–Vis irradiation (300 W Xe lamp), the best solvothermal composite (5%Mo-Fe3S4@TiO2) reached ∼30 μmol H2 h–1 after 3 h irradiation, corresponding to 25 times the rate of bare TiO2. For the microwave-derived series, the 7.5%Mo-Fe3S4@TiO2 composite delivered ∼29 μmol H2 h–1 after 3 h, corresponding to 24 times higher than bare TiO2, and 5 times higher than undoped Fe3S4@TiO2. Overall, Mo-doped Fe3S4 emerges as an earth-abundant, non-noble metal co-catalyst platform that significantly improves photocatalytic HER with TiO2 while maintaining performance under a time-efficient synthesis protocol.

title: Indoor Organic Solar Cells: Toward Enhancing Indoor Light Energy Harvesting Using Non-Fullerene Acceptors
content:
Abstract
This study investigates the performance and stability of organic solar cells (OSCs) employing nonfullerene acceptors (NFAs) under indoor light-emitting diode (LED) illumination. Using PM6 as the polymer donor and comparing PC70BM fullerene with ITIC-M, Y6-O, and Y7 NFAs, devices were fabricated and characterized electrically and optically. Under an illumination of 1500 lx LED light, power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) reached up to 20% with ITIC-M, outperforming the other acceptors. Electrical modeling using a single-diode equivalent circuit correlated experimental data with transport and recombination mechanisms, revealing that NFAs and fullerene-based devices exhibit distinct degradation pathways. Stability tests under continuous 1000 lx LED exposure showed that PM6:ITIC-M devices retained over 96% of their initial PCE after 511 h, indicating superior operational stability. The results demonstrate that NFA-based OSCs, particularly PM6:ITIC-M, are promising candidates for efficient, stable, and cost-effective indoor photovoltaic energy harvesting, suitable for powering low-energy devices.

title: Regulating Polysulfide Conversion on Fe-N  x   Single-Atom Catalysts Supported on Graphitic Carbon Nitride Revealed by Semi-In Situ XPS of Li–S Batteries
content:
Abstract
Lithium–sulfur batteries are limited by the polysulfide shuttle effect and sluggish conversion kinetics, both strongly influenced by the catalytic interface that mediates the polysulfide redox process. This work centers on the controlled synthesis of single-atom catalysts to establish how the local coordination environment dictates sulfur redox kinetics. We show that engineering the support prior to metal incorporation, rather than the metal site alone, is an effective and reproducible lever for tuning Fe-Nx single-atom catalysis on urea-derived graphitic carbon nitride. Thermal reduction of the support before Fe loading reshapes the resulting Fe-Nx coordination environment, yielding atomically dispersed, coordinatively unsaturated sites with mixed Fe2+/Fe3+ valence and no detectable aggregation, as established by X-ray absorption spectroscopy and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Extended X-ray absorption fine structure analysis reveals lower average Fe-N coordination numbers on the reduced support. Density functional theory further demonstrates the catalytic role of atomically dispersed Fe sites by predicting stronger polysulfide adsorption and lower conversion barriers relative to the metal-free gCN support. To resolve how these sites act during operation, we track sulfur speciation across extended cycling using semi-in situ sulfur 2p X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, which reveals pronounced enrichment of reduced sulfur species and suppression of oxidized intermediates, direct spectroscopic evidence of accelerated polysulfide conversion. The reduced-support catalysts also show improved durability (∼71–75 vs ∼48% capacity retention for the bare support). Together, these results establish thermal reduction as a controllable design principle for single-atom catalysts in lithium–sulfur batteries and semi-in situ X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy as a powerful probe of sulfur redox mechanisms.

title: A Zero-Conductive-Additive Covalent Organic Polymer Cathode for High-Temperature Lithium-Ion Batteries with High Stability
content:
Abstract
Li-ion batteries (LIBs) capable of sustaining high-temperature cycling are essential for energy storage; however, building cathode materials with stable cycling for long term at high temperatures remains a significant challenge. Organic cathode materials have significant applied implications for LIBs; however, they are limited by low electronic conductivity, which requires a large amount of inactive conductive carbon for electrode fabrication, leading to a significant decrease in energy density. Herein, we demonstrated that a π-conjugated covalent organic polymer (COP) cathode, coupled with ether-based electrolytes containing 2 wt % LiNO3 additives, could act as an ultra-stable conductive-additive-free organic cathode for lithium storage at room and high temperatures. Typically, at 60 °C, the conductive-additive-free COP cathode could deliver a high initial reversible capacity (374 mAh g–1), an unprecedented cyclability for 5000 cycles (0.01% capacity decay per cycle), and a promising rate capability. The π-conjugated framework of this COP promises enhanced electronic conductivity with high mechanical and chemical stability. The ether-based electrolyte shows favorable compatibility with the cathode and yields a stable cathode–electrolyte interface (CEI) with LiF as an ionic-conductor component to facilitate Li+ transport.

title: Surface Engineering of CsPbBr 3  Perovskite Photoanodes with Zeolitic Imidazolate Frameworks for Sustainable Oxygen Evolution
content:
Abstract
The aqueous instability of inorganic halide perovskites such as CsPbBr3 remains a critical barrier to their practical utilization in photoelectrochemical water splitting. Here, we employ surface engineering with zeolitic imidazolate frameworks (ZIFs) to simultaneously stabilize CsPbBr3 photoanodes and modulate their interfacial charge-transfer behavior. By systematically comparing Zn-based ZIF-8 and Co-based ZIF-9 overlayers, we distinguish hydrolytic protection from interfacial charge-transfer effects and demonstrate how the metal-node coordination environment governs photoelectrode performance. Although both framework coatings enhance surface hydrophobicity and effectively suppress moisture-induced degradation, they exhibit distinct electronic characteristics. ZIF-8 functions primarily as an insulating passivation layer that suppresses surface recombination but impedes hole transfer because of its high interfacial charge-transfer resistance. In contrast, the Co-based coordination network in ZIF-9 establishes a favorable interfacial heterojunction that lowers the interfacial charge-transfer resistance and facilitates hole extraction toward the oxygen evolution reaction. Consequently, the FTO/TiO2/CsPbBr3/ZIF-9 photoanode delivers a photocurrent density of 2.7 mA cm–2 at 1.23 V vs. RHE, representing an approximately 89% enhancement over the ZIF-8-modified counterpart (1.43 mA cm–2), while retaining more than 75% of its initial photocurrent after 7200 s of continuous illumination. These findings demonstrate that rational surface engineering with MOF overlayers provides a viable strategy for simultaneously enhancing surface protection and interfacial charge transport in perovskite-based photoelectrodes for solar fuel applications.

title: Can Carbon Coating Improve the Durability of Carbon Xerogels as Catalyst Supports for Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cell Electrodes?
content:
Abstract
A carbon xerogel (CX) with a pore size of ∼70 nm was selected as support for a fuel cell electrocatalyst. While carbon xerogels offer excellent mass transport properties, their amorphous nature reduces their resistance to carbon corrosion under the oxidizing conditions of PEMFC operation. To tackle this, a partially graphitized carbon layer was deposited on the xerogel surface using chemical vapor deposition (CVD). This layer covers a large part of the micropores but keeps intact the interconnected meso/macropore network of the CX. The carbon-coated CX was also post-treated at 1500 °C under an inert atmosphere for further crystallization. Pt nanoparticles (20 wt %) were then deposited on both pristine and CVD-treated CXs by reduction of hexachloroplatinic acid in liquid phase; the resulting catalysts were evaluated with respect to their electrochemical activity and compared to a commercial carbon black-supported catalyst. The catalyst on the post-treated supports exhibited initial catalytic activities comparable to those obtained on pristine CX. After accelerated aging in RDE configuration, despite a decrease in the catalytic surface of Pt, specific activities increased while mass activities remained stable. In the Membrane-Electrodes Assembly configuration, the catalyst supported on the carbon xerogel post-treated with chemical vapor deposition and subsequent high-temperature treatment at 1500 °C exhibited encouraging durability behavior. This behavior was attributed to differences in Pt nanoparticle growth on post-treated carbon xerogel supports. Moreover, it was observed that these post-treatments do not negatively affect mass transport inside the electrode, since the meso/macropore texture remained intact.

title: Elucidating the Role of sALD-Deposited ZrO  x   Coatings on the Electrochemical Performance of LiNi 0.5 Mn 1.5 O 4  Cathodes
content:
Abstract
LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4 (LNMO) is a promising high-voltage, cobalt-free cathode material but suffers from severe interfacial degradation that limits the cycling stability of LNMO/graphite cells. Here, spatial atomic layer deposition (sALD) was employed to deposit conformal nano-ZrOx coatings directly onto LNMO composite electrodes, providing a scalable approach for electrode-level interface engineering. The influence of coating thickness and substrate translation speed on electrochemical performance was systematically investigated. Increasing the ZrOx thickness improved the long-term stability of LNMO/graphite cells but increased interfacial resistance, highlighting the trade-off between interfacial protection and charge-transfer kinetics. A ZrOx thickness of 3.0 nm provided the optimum balance, extending cell end-of-life by 71% compared with pristine LNMO while maintaining good rate capability. Post-mortem X-ray fluorescence analysis revealed reduced Mn and Ni deposition on graphite anodes, consistent with suppressed cathode–anode cross-talk. Furthermore, reducing the substrate translation speed from 10 to 5 mm s–1 further increased the end-of-life of the LNMO/graphite cells by 51%. These results demonstrate that both coating thickness and sALD processing parameters are critical for developing durable, high-voltage LNMO/graphite cells.

title: Investigation of IrRuO x -Based Porous Transport Electrodes as a Function of Post-Treatments
content:
Abstract
This study examines the effects of post-treatment annealing (argon, vacuum, air; 200–500 °C) on electrodeposited IrRuOx porous transport electrodes (PTEs) using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM-EDS). The aim is to investigate how these treatments influence the material's composition, structure, and their respective impact on electrochemical properties. Electrochemical testing reveals atmosphere-dependent pathways: argon annealing improves stability up to 400 °C but produces Ir enrichment and heterogeneity at 500 °C that degrades performance; air annealing stabilizes oxidized species at 200 °C but yields larger activity and stability losses by 300 °C; and vacuum annealing at 200 °C preserves activity while improving stability. XPS characterization focuses on the analysis of Ir 4f, Ru 3d, and O 1s regions. For Ir 4f and Ru 3d spectra, simple metrics that didn’t involve fitting are explored, whereas for O 1s, deconvolution strategies are evaluated and a six-component model is adopted. In many cases, simple XPS metrics, binding energy (BE) and full width at half maximum (FWHM), capture trends that correlate with catalytic activity and stability, while detailed fitting is necessary to resolve complex oxygen speciation in other cases. Additionally, XPS-derived metrics are correlated with electrochemical performance using principal component analysis (PCA), highlighting patterns within a complex dataset. These results advance our understanding of XPS analysis of Ir-based catalysts, emphasize the importance of thorough and careful analysis, and highlight opportunities for combining simple metrics with multivariate analysis for the development of more efficient materials.

title: Cu2S Wires With Controllable Thickness on Li Foil for Stable and High‐Performance Lithium Metal Anodes
content:
Cu2S wires with controllable thickness are synthesized through a simple electrodeposition process and transferred onto lithium metal by mechanical rolling. The transferred Cu2S wires form an ultralow‐resistance interphase that reduces the SEI resistance, thereby enabling uniform Li plating and stripping. Consequently, the Cu2S wire‐modified Li anode delivers outstanding stability in both symmetric and full cells.








ABSTRACT
Lithium (Li) metal is an attractive anode for next‐generation high‐energy‐density batteries. However, its practical implementation is limited by interfacial instability and dendritic growth, often accompanied by high interfacial resistance. In this study, a strategy combining electrodeposition with a mechanical rolling process is presented to lower the interfacial resistance and suppress Li dendrite growth. By adjusting the current density, the thickness of Cu2S wires is controlled at a fixed synthesis duration. A Cu foil bearing 0.32 µm thick Cu2S wires is rolled with a Li foil, transferring the wires onto the Li surface to form Li@Cu2S wire. During rolling, spontaneous lithiation generates a Li2S‐rich solid electrolyte interphase embedded with three‐dimensional Cu dots. Li@Cu2S wire symmetric cells exhibit stable Li plating/stripping for >3500 h at 1 mA cm−2 and 1 mAh cm−2. Moreover, Li@Cu2S wire∥LiFePO4 full cells retain more than 95% of the initial capacity for over 450 cycles at 1 C, demonstrating outstanding electrochemical performance. This work provides a simple and effective approach to enhancing Li anode performance through interfacial engineering.

title: Decoding Perovskite Crystallization Dynamics Via Absorption‐Normalized In‐Situ Photoluminescence: A Case Study on the Role of Humidity
content:
An in‐situ spectroscopy platform is developed that tracks both photoluminescence (PL) and UV–vis absorption during perovskite thin‐film fabrication, enabling capture of absorption‐normalized PL in‐situ. This decouples radiative efficiency from emitter amount. Applying this to humidified processing, we find that non‐radiative recombination pathways that develop at the early stage of film formation are the origin of device performance impairment.








ABSTRACT
Real‐time photoluminescence (PL) spectroscopy is widely used to probe crystallization kinetics and defect evolution during perovskite film formation. However, as both the amount of emissive material and its radiative ability evolve during crystallization and both influence the raw PL intensity, their contributions must be decoupled to properly interpret the nanostructure development of perovskite thin films. Here, we develop an in‐situ spectroscopy platform that enables tracking both of PL and UV–vis absorption during spin coating and thermal annealing, allowing the PL intensity to be normalized by the absorption at the excitation wavelength. This normalization decouples intrinsic radiative efficiency from emitter amount in the wet film, providing a rigorous metric for monitoring non radiative recombination in real time. Applying this method, we find that humidity does not simply alter crystallization kinetics but actively hijacks the early‐stage pathway by stabilizing intermediate species that persist after annealing, which directly correlates with suppressed absorption‐normalized PL intensity and degraded device performance. This work establishes absorption‑normalized in‑situ PL as a powerful and potentially widely applicable diagnostic tool for monitoring perovskite thin‑film development and beyond.

title: Axial Cl‐Coordinated Porous FeCoZn Trimetallic Single‐Atom Catalysts: Breaking the Linear Scaling Relation for Superior Oxygen Reduction Reaction and Ultrastable Zinc‐Air Batteries
content:
Porous trimetallic single‐atom catalysts (TACs) with Fe/Co/Zn co‐shared N coordination and axial Zn‐Cl coordination are synthesized via ZIF‐8‐derived ion exchange and gas etching. The trimetallic single atoms and axial coordination of Cl on Zn facilitate bridge‐type adsorption of O2 and break linear scaling relationship to boosts oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) catalytic activity and cycle life of zinc‐air batteries (ZABs).








ABSTRACT
Single‐atom catalysts (SACs) have emerged as a research frontier in electrocatalysis. However, conventional SACs possess single metal active sites, which hardly break the symmetry of geometric and electronic structure of M–N4. To address this limitation, porous trimetallic single‐atom catalysts (TACs) is fabricated via ZIF‐8‐derived ion exchange and gas‐phase etching methods. The catalyst features Fe, Co, and Zn single atoms with a special M–N4 configuration where the three metal atoms share one N ligand. And axial coordination structure exists between Zn and Cl atoms. It exhibits outstanding oxygen reduction activity and stability under acidic/alkaline conditions, with a half‐wave potential of 0.81 V/0.96 V and loss of 4 mV/8 mV after 30 000 cycles. Only 6.5% performance decay is observed after 2163 h of charge‐discharge cycling in zinc‐air batteries (ZABs). Physicochemical characterization and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the trimetallic configuration breaks the geometric and electronic structural symmetry, optimizing the adsorption of intermediates during the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). Axial coordination of Cl on Zn facilitates the bridge‐type adsorption of O2 and breaks the linear scaling relationship. This work offers a novel strategy to break the symmetry of geometric and electronic structure of SACs and regulate reaction pathways.

title: A Tailored Multifunctional Lithium Organosilicate Salt Constructing Robust Interphases for High Voltage Lithium Metal Batteries
content:
A fluorinated lithium organosilicate salt, lithium fluorobis(fluoropinacolatoborato)silicate (LiPBS), is designed and synthesized. It forms a rigid‐flexible cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI) on the cathode and an inorganic‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) on the anode, effectively scavenges HF/H2O, and greatly enhances the high‐voltage cycling stability of Li metal batteries under elevated temperatures, outperforming conventional LiPF6.








ABSTRACT
Lithium metal batteries (LMBs) have attracted extensive attention due to their high energy density. However, when lithium (Li) metal is paired with high‐voltage cathode materials, its practical application is limited by issues such as continuous oxidative decomposition of electrolytes and the incompatibility between electrolytes and aggressive electrodes. Herein, we synthesize a fluorinated lithium organosilicate salt (i.e., lithium fluorobis(fluoropinacolatoborato)silicate, LiPBS) to address the aforementioned challenges. The results show that the LiPBS can form a protective and rigid‐flexible cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI) on the cathode surface. Simultaneously, PBS− readily forms a coordination ion pair (CIP) with Li+, constructing an inorganic‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) on the Li anode. Furthermore, Si─O groups in the LiPBS can effectively scavenge HF and H2O from the electrolyte. These advantageous properties enable LiCoO2 (LCO, 1.89 mAh cm−2)/Li (50 µm) coin and pouch cells to exhibit excellent cycling performance at high voltages and elevated rates‒for example, retaining 82% capacity after 250 cycles at 1 C and 4.5 V, compared to 80% retention after only 67 cycles for the LiPF6‐based counterpart. This performance is maintained even at an elevated temperature of 50°C. This work highlights the crucial role of lithium organosilicate salt in determining the electrochemical performance of LMBs.

title: Tracing and Healing Multiscale Defects for Cost‐Effective Lithium Carbonate‐Derived Layered Oxide Cathodes
content:
Lithium carbonate is far cheaper than lithium hydroxide, but the resulting layered oxide cathodes suffer from inferior electrochemical performance. This work traces the origin of this gap and unveils multiscale defects rooted in the solid‐, liquid‐, and gas‐phase features of the carbonate pathway. A single secondary heat treatment heals these defects, delivering hydroxide‐level performance at a 9%–16% lower lithium precursor cost.








ABSTRACT
Lithium carbonate (LC) is markedly cheaper than lithium hydroxide (LH) but remains underused for layered oxide cathodes because LC‐derived materials perform poorly. Here, using a mid‐Ni cathode, LiNi0.65Co0.05Mn0.30O2 (N65), we trace this performance gap to LC‐induced defects that span length scales, from atomic‐scale disorder to nanoscale and microscale porosity. These defects originate from three features of the carbonate pathway that act across the solid, liquid, and gas phases, namely decoupled dehydration and lithiation, late melting of the carbonate, and a locally oxygen‐deficient atmosphere from evolving CO2. Guided by this picture, we heal the defects with a single secondary heat treatment (SH) that adds an optimized amount of LH, simultaneously replenishing lithium, restoring an oxidizing atmosphere, and densifying the structure. The resulting N65‐LC SH achieves discharge capacity, rate capability, and cycling stability comparable to those of the LH counterpart, while cutting the lithium precursor cost by 9% to 16% relative to conventional all‐LH synthesis. More broadly, the gap between LH and LC is not an intrinsic property of the carbonate but a consequence of a precursor‐specific pathway that, once traced, can be engineered around to unlock low‐cost, high‐performance Ni‐based layered oxide cathodes.
