title: In Situ Defect Engineering of Atomically Dispersed Iridium on Mesoporous Mixed Oxide Frameworks for Robust PEM Water Electrolysis
content:
An in situ acid‐etching‐assisted defect engineering strategy establishes a highly electron‐deficient, rigid Ir‐O‐Ce covalent framework that thermodynamically locks lattice oxygen, enabling exceptionally active and ultra‐durable acidic oxygen evolution. This architecture firmly anchors atomically dispersed Ir species through strong metal‐support interaction. The resulting electron‐deficient Ir centers deliver exceptionally active and durable acidic oxygen evolution for sustainable water electrolysis. 








ABSTRACT
Reconciling exceptional catalytic activity with operational durability at ultralow noble‐metal loadings remains a central challenge for proton exchange membrane water electrolysis. Herein, an in situ acid‐etching‐assisted defect engineering strategy is reported for constructing an ultrahigh‐loading electrocatalyst (Ir@CM4) that predominantly features atomically dispersed iridium anchored on hierarchical mesoporous CeMn oxides. Directional Mn dissolution generates a dense oxygen vacancy network that traps Ir species, inducing a profound strong metal‐support interaction to establish a highly electron‐deficient, rigid Ir‐O‐Ce covalent framework. Consequently, Ir@CM4 delivers an exceptional mass activity of 948.15 A g−1 at 1.53 V versus RHE (31‐fold higher than commercial Ir Black). In a PEMWE full cell with an ultralow loading of 0.28 mgIr cm−2, it sustains robust operation for 6350 h at an industrial‐relevant 1 A cm−2. Multimodal in situ tracking confirms that this covalent rigidity thermodynamically locks lattice oxygen, bypassing degradation‐prone pathways to strictly enforce the highly stable adsorbate evolution mechanism. Density functional theory uncovers the quantum‐mechanical origin: strong metal‐support interaction‐induced charge transfer downshifts the Ir d‐band center to ‐3.93 eV, which circumvents traditional scaling relations by weakening antibonding orbital filling. This multiscale structural and electronic synergy effectively decouples the activity‐stability trade‐off, providing a translatable paradigm for industrial‐grade acidic water electrolysis.

title: Oxyhalide‐Derived Nb‐O‐Cl Interfacial Frameworks for Mitigating Oxygen‐Related Degradation and Facilitating Li+ Transport in High‐Voltage Ni‐Rich Cathodes
content:
A reconstructive Nb–O–Cl interfacial framework stabilizes the cathode/sulfide‐electrolyte interface of Ni‐rich NCM cathodes. The framework mitigates oxygen‐related degradation and O2 evolution, promotes continuous Li+ transport, and suppresses interfacial deterioration during cycling, thereby enabling a more stable high‐voltage all‐solid‐state battery interface.








ABSTRACT
High‐voltage Ni‐rich cathodes coupled with sulfide solid electrolytes suffer from coupled instability of highly oxidized Ni‐O configurations and Li+ transport discontinuity under deep delithiation. Conventional oxide coatings mainly act as passive barrier layers that separate reactive contacts but remain structurally isolated from layered cathodes without simultaneously regulating interfacial chemistry and Li+ transport. Here, we report an oxyhalide‐enabled interfacial chemistry strategy based on a reconstructive Nb‐O‐Cl framework on LiNi0.83Co0.07Mn0.10O2 cathodes (denoted as C‐NCM). Derived from a mixed‐anion LiNbOCl4 (LNOC) precursor, the Nb‐O‐Cl framework undergoes mechanochemically assisted interfacial reconstruction, forming an amorphous oxyhalide interphase coupled with a Nb‐containing near‐surface region. Unlike passive oxide barriers, this chemically integrated architecture simultaneously reshapes the local Ni‐O electronic environment and mediates interface‐crossing Li+ transport. Nb‐O/Nb‐O‐Cl coordination redistributes local charge and is associated with improved retention of highly oxidized Ni‐O configurations and mitigated oxygen‐related irreversible evolution, while the Cl‐containing oxyhalide framework provides an ionically conductive transition region that facilitates Li+ migration across the cathode/electrolyte interface. Accordingly, C‐NCM exhibits reduced sulfide‐derived interphase formation and slower resistance growth, together with 88.17% capacity retention after 500 cycles at 4.5 V under high cathode loading. This work shifts cathode/sulfide‐electrolyte interface design from passive oxide‐barrier protection toward reconstructive mixed‐anion interfacial chemistry.

title:
Radical–Electrochemical
Coupling Enables Amination
of Methane
content:
Abstract
The selective functionalization of methane under ambient conditions is widely regarded as a holy grail in chemistry, yet remains fundamentally limited not only by the inertness of the C–H bond but also by the transient nature of highly reactive intermediates. Short-lived species are often difficult to preserve and utilize prior to productive coupling, constraining accessible reaction pathways and product selectivity. Here, we establish a reaction framework based on in situ interfacial interception of reactive radicals, enabling the temporal coordination between radical lifetime and subsequent reaction processes. Plasma generates short-lived methyl radicals in immediate proximity to a gas–electrode interface, allowing their direct delivery and capture at the catalytic surface, while the electrochemical interface independently converts ammonia into surface-bound amino intermediates. Their coupling enables selective C–N bond formation. This spatially and temporally coordinated process allows highly reactive radical species to be synchronized with interfacial reaction steps, facilitating their productive utilization. Guided by density functional theory, we identify a nickel–cobalt layered double hydroxide catalyst that promotes interfacial coupling between *CH3 and *NH2 intermediates. The optimized system achieves a Faradaic efficiency of 54% for methylamine at 10 mA cm–2, with a productivity of 201 μmol cm–2 h–1 under ambient conditions. Beyond methane amination, this work demonstrates that coordinating the lifetime and transformation of reactive intermediates provides a generalizable strategy for catalytic control, offering new opportunities for the activation and selective transformation of inert molecules.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
Photobiocatalytic Diastereo-
and Enantioselective
Synthesis of Noncanonical Amino Acids Bearing Challenging Stereochemical
Dyads and Triads
content:
Abstract
Catalyst-controlled stereodivergent synthesis of acyclic molecules bearing multiple stereogenic centers remains a longstanding challenge in asymmetric catalysis, particularly through intermolecular radical C–C coupling. Here, we report the directed evolution of pyridoxal 5′-phosphate (PLP)-dependent biocatalysts for the stereodivergent synthesis of noncanonical amino acids bearing either skipped α,γ-stereochemical dyads or contiguous α,β,γ-stereochemical triads. Starting from a thermophilic tryptophan synthase β-subunit, protein engineering generated complementary enzyme variants that selectively construct three of the four possible α,γ-stereoisomers through biocatalyst-controlled reversal of both remote γ-stereochemistry and proximal α-stereochemistry. These engineered enzymes catalyzed intermolecular radical C–C bond formation with a broad range of secondary alkyltrifluoroborates, affording α,γ-disubstituted amino acids in excellent yields and stereoselectivities. Furthermore, directed evolution enabled efficient β-dehydroxylative radical coupling of the non-native threonine-derived aminoacrylate intermediate, providing amino acids bearing contiguous α,β,γ-stereochemical triads with up to 96:4:<0.1:<0.1 d.r. and >99:1 e.r. To further demonstrate the synthetic utility of this platform, the stereochemically enriched amino acids were transformed into valuable γ-chiral amines through engineered PLP-dependent tryptophan decarboxylases, establishing a dual PLP enzyme-based biocatalytic cascade for the enantiodivergent synthesis of privileged amine scaffolds. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that enzyme-controlled γ-stereoselectivity originates from active-site remodeling that modulates π–π interactions and steric contacts governing the facial selectivity of the radical addition step. This work expands the synthetic capabilities of radical biocatalysis by enabling catalyst-controlled stereodivergent assembly of complex acyclic stereochemical arrays and establishes engineered PLP enzymes as versatile catalysts for the synthesis of stereochemically complex amino acids and chiral amines.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
Dead-Potassium
Activation Reconstructing Stabilized
Interface Enables Stable Anode-Free Potassium Metal Batteries
content:
Abstract
Anode-free high-energy-density potassium metal batteries (AFPMBs) are critically constrained by the irreversible accumulation of dead potassium (K) and severe dendrite growth. These issues stem from sluggish interfacial kinetics and the continuous fracture of the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). A multifunctional electrolyte engineering strategy is proposed by incorporating bismuth iodide (BiI3) into a carbonate-based system to simultaneously regulate the bulk K+ solvation sheath, reconstruct the interfacial solvation structure, and reactivate dead K. Experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that the iodide/triiodide (I–/I3–) species weaken the coordination of K+ with solvents and FSI– in the bulk electrolyte, generating a weakly coordinated solvation structure, which facilitates K+ desolvation. At the electrode interface, Bi-derived sites preferentially recruit and selectively adsorb free FSI– over carbonate solvents and promote their enrichment toward the inner Helmholtz layer, thereby reconstructing an anion-rich interfacial solvation structure that directs the formation of a robust inorganic-rich SEI. In parallel, the reversible I–/I3– redox couple can reactivate dead K. Benefiting from the synergistic suppression of dendrite growth, reduction of irreversible K loss, and enhancement of interfacial kinetics, the symmetric cells demonstrate stable cycling for over 1300 h at 0.5 mA cm–2 and 0.5 mAh cm–2. AFPMBs also demonstrate markedly improved cycling stability and capacity retention in the carbonate-based electrolyte. This work provides a foundation for designing advanced electrolyte additives to enhance electrochemical stability in AFPMBs.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
A Molecular Switch
with Dual Responses to Electrochemical
and Mechanical Stimuli
content:
Abstract
Molecular switches capable of responding to two or more orthogonal stimuli are essential for advancing molecular-scale logic, sensing, and memory technologies. However, integrating distinct control mechanisms within a single-molecule architecture remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we report a single-molecule electrochemical-mechanical dual-control switch based on difluoroboron dipyrromethene (BODIPY) molecular junctions. We demonstrate that applying an electrochemical gate voltage threshold (−0.6 V) reduces the BODIPY core to a stable radical anion, effectively serving as a logic enable (EN) signal. Under this electrochemically activated regime, precision mechanical modulation (∼5.0 Å amplitude) via an STM tip cleanly dictates the molecular conformation. Compressive strain drives the formation of a highly conductive asymmetric Au–S/Au−π contact (the SET operation) with a two-order-of-magnitude conductance contrast, while tensile strain physically ruptures the Au−π interfacial coupling to recover the symmetric terminal Au–S anchoring (the RESET operation). This dual-input sliding molecular resistor operates stably at frequencies up to 200 Hz, with density functional theory calculations elucidating the underlying radical-enhanced resonant transport pathway. By seamlessly mapping these synergistic electro-mechanical inputs to digital logic, we successfully transform this molecular junction into a nonvolatile, nanoscale gated RS latch. Ultimately, our work establishes a highly robust and versatile design strategy for constructing complex, multistimuli-responsive molecular circuitry at the single-molecule limit.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
Water–Organic
Interfaces Drive Molecular Evolution
from Squalene to Steroids
content:
Abstract
In living cells, the conversion of squalene to lanosterol requires two dedicated enzymes and proceeds through 2,3-oxidosqualene as an essential intermediate. We show that water microdroplets contacting immiscible organic solvents accomplish this same multistep transformation without enzymatic catalysis. We propose that the oriented electric field across the water–organic interface generates reactive oxygen species that epoxidize squalene and then initiates acid-catalyzed ring-opening of the epoxide followed by a cationic polyene cyclization cascade to yield lanosterol. H218O labeling traced oxygen from water into TEMPO-derived and peroxyacetate ions observed by real-time mass spectrometry. LC–HRMS/MS further revealed C18–C30 reaction products with spectral matches to oxygenated terpenoid and steroid-like structures. We find that ethyl acetate is the most effective organic solvent because it generates peroxyacetic acid at the interface. Simulations show that a preformed protonated 2,3-oxidosqualene model remains hydrated and oriented after placement at the ethyl acetate–water interface, and calculations on microsolvation models indicate that an interfacial water configuration preferentially stabilizes the epoxidation transition state relative to the reactant by approximately 3 kcal mol–1. These results establish a plausible, abiotic pathway for steroid emergence and diversification at water–organic interfaces.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
Subcrystal-Mediated
Hetero-Crystallization Enables
Phase-Controlled Zeolite Intergrowths with Multidimensional Disorder
content:
Abstract
Phase-controlled synthesis and comprehensive structural understanding of intergrowth zeolites remain challenging because of kinetic competition during crystallization and oversimplified structural models. Differences in nucleation kinetics between competing frameworks and framework interconversion during crystallization can decouple the initial synthesis composition from the final phase composition, while conventional stacking models cannot fully describe their structural complexity. Here, we develop a subcrystal-mediated heterocrystallization strategy using highly active ZSM-5 (MFI) and ZSM-11 (MEL) subcrystals (<10 nm) as preorganized building units. Mixing the isolated ZSM-5 and ZSM-11 subcrystals at defined ratios under mild conditions bypasses the kinetic bias associated with the faster ZSM-5 nucleation and suppresses framework interconversion, enabling ratio-directed control over MFI/MEL phase composition. Time-resolved crystallization and persistently low concentrations of soluble species support a predominantly particle-attachment-dominated nonclassical pathway rather than extensive dissolution-regrowth. Atomic-resolution imaging combined with T12-unit analysis resolves multidimensional disorder beyond conventional one-dimensional intergrowth models, revealing two-dimensional structural disorder, diverse channel architectures, corresponding connector motifs, and connected or interrupted interfaces that accommodate 90°-rotated intergrowth. Variations in phase composition are accompanied by systematic changes in pore characteristics and acidity, together with tunable molecular diffusion and catalytic behavior. This combined control of crystallization kinetics and multidimensional structural complexity provides a general platform for engineering intergrown zeolites with tailored functionalities.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
Dual-Polyhedral Distortion
for Low-Cost Amorphous
Halide Electrolytes with Improved Ionic Conductivity
content:
Abstract
Amorphous halide solid electrolytes (AHSEs) have emerged as promising candidates for high-performance all-solid-state Na batteries (ASSNBs) owing to their balanced comprehensive performance. However, rational design principles assisting the precursor selection are still limited for developing low-cost Na-based AHSEs with improved ionic conductivity. Herein, a series of low-cost AHSEs, xNaBF4–ZrCl4 (x = 0.3, 0.5, 1, and 2), were synthesized via a one-step mechanochemical process. Competitive coordination between the Zr4+ and B3+ cations under mechanochemical activation is proposed to promote the rearrangement of F– and Cl– anions within the halide framework. The resulting dual-distorted polyhedral coordination facilitates the formation of long-range disordered structures that are highly favorable for isotropic Na+ transport, exhibiting a high Na+ ionic conductivity up to 1.01 mS cm–1 at 30 °C with excellent oxidative stability of 4.33 V vs Na+/Na. When assembled into all-solid-state cells, the 0.5NaBF4–ZrCl4 electrolyte enables stable cycling between 2.5 and 4.2 V with a capacity retention of 71.5% after 400 cycles at 0.2 C rate. This work provides a novel design paradigm for AHSEs and highlights the promising potential of high-performance ASSNBs.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
Simultaneous Installation
of 1,6-Stereocenters by
Asymmetric Allylation of Resorcinol Boronates: Application to the
Synthesis of Merocyclophane A
content:
Abstract
Installing multiple noncontiguous stereocenters in a single catalytic event offers a powerful platform for constructing complex three-dimensional molecular architectures, yet asymmetric methodologies capable of selectively forging remote 1,n-stereochemical relationships remain limited. Here we disclose a strategy for the simultaneous installation of 1,6-stereocenters via para-selective activation of chiral resorcinol boronates with π-allyl iridium complexes. Upon oxidation-induced rearomatization, the resulting dearomatized intermediates furnish the allylated products in an overall transformation that exhibits excellent regio- and stereoselectivity. Crucially, independent variation of the ligand and boronic ester configuration provides predictable access to all four stereoisomers with no observable match–mismatch effects. The synthetic potential of the methodology is exemplified by a concise total synthesis of the cyanobacteria-derived [7.7]paracyclophane merocyclophane A, in which all stereocenters are installed simultaneously on the resorcinol core in a single step.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
Möbius Aromatic
Figure-Eight Knotted Three-Dimensional
Covalent Organic Frameworks
content:
Abstract
Möbius aromaticity extends the concept of aromaticity into the topological dimension. However, the synthesis of well-defined molecular systems with this unique property, especially the assembly into infinite polymeric networks, remains a significant challenge due to uncontrolled ring-strain effects. Herein, we report the synthesis of a Möbius aromatic hexa[2,3-thienylene] macrocycle (HTE) with a striking figure-eight shape and the control sample of tetra[2,3-thienylene] (TTE) with an antiaromatic nature, which is further assembled into the extended 3D covalent organic frameworks (COFs) of NUST-67 and NUST-66. The Möbius aromaticity of HTE can modulate the oxidation potential, lower the p-band center of active sites, and weaken the adsorption strength of the *OOH intermediate. As a result, the obtained NUST-67, with a thermodynamically optimized reaction pathway and kinetically enhanced mass/charge transfer, exhibits much superior electrocatalytic activity and selectivity toward H2O2 reduction with industrial-grade performance than NUST-66, featuring a current density window of 100–400 mA cm–2 and an H2O2 Faradic efficiency exceeding 88%. This study discloses the first integration of a Möbius aromatic unit into a COF and elucidates the working effect of aromaticity by a targeted electrocatalytic probe, which establishes a new paradigm for designing organic electrocatalysts by aromaticity engineering.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
Dynamic
Extraction of Internal Active Species in Liquid
Metal-Based Biphasic Catalyst
content:
Abstract
Catalyst development is pivotal for industrial and energy advancements, yet it is fundamentally challenged by the static nature of the conventional solid catalysts. Their active sites, locked within rigid frameworks, are neither dynamically responsive nor regenerable, leading to an irreversible consumption during reaction cycles. Herein, we report an electrocapillary-enhanced dynamic extraction process to design a liquid metal-based biphasic catalyst (LMBC), enabling precise population control and in situ regeneration of active species. We establish two key thermodynamic criteria for the dynamic extraction mechanism to guide the LMBC development: alloying energy, which governs the tendency of active elements to form solid active alloys within the liquid metal matrix (gallium, Ga), and surface energy, which drives the dynamic extraction and surface exposure of internal active alloys. Through this mechanism, the quantity of exposed active species becomes adaptively adjustable, allowing fine-tuned control over the catalytic activity. Moreover, deactivated species can be replenished in situ from the liquid metal interior. This LMBC platform demonstrates universality and scalability in the alloy composition across diverse catalysis systems. Overall, this work provides a novel strategy for designing adaptive renewable catalytic systems.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
When
Organic Chemistry Meets Surface Science: From
Nanographene Characterization to Single-Molecule Reactions
content:
Abstract
The interplay between organic chemistry and surface science allows for atomically precise characterization, synthesis, and manipulation of carbon-based nanostructures. Advances in scanning probe microscopy and on-surface synthesis have unlocked new routes to obtaining fascinating nanographenes, exotic and highly reactive molecules, and controlled single-molecule reactions. Importantly, these developments open access to transformations that are inaccessible to solution-phase chemistry. Here, we illustrate the potential of this approach and outline the future opportunities and challenges.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
Toward the Rational
Design of Tailored Ligands for
Intrinsically Disordered Proteins through NMR
content:
Abstract
Understanding the driving forces governing the interactions between intrinsically disordered proteins and their potential ligands represents a key step toward the rational design of drugs targeting this type of proteins. Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy provides a unique opportunity to achieve detailed atom-resolved information toward this ambitious goal. We present here a set of differently functionalized calix[4]arene-based multivalent ligands designed to target different regions of the well-characterized intrinsically disordered protein α-synuclein. Dedicated NMR experiments extended the analysis from backbone to side-chain nuclear spins, thus enabling the atom-resolved identification of short-range contacts between the calixarene ligands and methyl or aromatic groups of the protein surface, and revealing how these interactions refine the electrostatically driven association within different lysine-rich motifs. This approach provides a comprehensive description of how the macrocycles recognize and bind the target protein, offering a basis for the rational design of ligands capable of modulating protein function.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
One-Pot Hierarchical
Assembly of Simple Molecules
to Vinylene- and Indole-Linked Covalent Organic Frameworks
content:
Abstract
The development in the synthesis of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) has been oriented toward the integration of simplicity, accessibility, stability, diversity, and functionality. However, a central bottleneck remains the lack of effective strategies for assembling simple, unsymmetric, and readily available molecules into highly ordered frameworks. Here, we report a practical synthesis of robust, diversified, and functional COFs via one-pot assembly from a low-cost and simple-structured molecule, 4-methyl-3-nitrobenzonitrile (MNBN). Leveraging the versatile but orthogonal reactivities of MNBN, a three-step cascade sequence, including nitrile cyclotrimerization, Knoevenagel condensation, and reductive cyclization, achieved the symmetrization, reticulation, and functionalization in one pot, thereby enabling the hierarchical construction of two series of COFs with stable o-nitrostyrene or indole linkages. The resulting COFs displayed high crystallinity, permanent porosity, and exceptional stability; solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (SSNMR) experiments combined with selective isotopic-labeling synthesis further confirmed the high selectivity and controllability of the hierarchical assembly. Notably, the indole-linked COFs, featuring conjugated and electron-rich frameworks, displayed emergent photoelectronic properties and served as efficient, reusable catalysts in both metal-free photocatalytic and metallaphotoredox reactions. By hierarchically exploiting the intrinsic reactivity of a simple, unsymmetric molecule, this work bridges classical organic synthesis and cross-scale covalent assembly, achieving the programmable construction of stable, diversified, and functional COFs.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
A Dynamic Self-Reporting
Metal–Organic Framework
System for Catalysis and Real-Time Reaction Monitoring
content:
Abstract
Modern catalysis research has primarily focused on improving catalyst activity, selectivity, and stability through active-site engineering, microenvironment regulation, and mechanistic understanding. However, the sustainability and efficiency of catalytic processes also depend on the dynamic evolution of reaction systems, including substrate consumption, catalyst deactivation, and product accumulation. Despite their importance, these changes are typically assessed by off-line analysis rather than real-time monitoring, which hinders efficient process optimization and sustainable operation. Here, we develop a dynamic self-reporting (DSR) catalytic system based on Ag@UiO-66-(COOH)2/NDCA that simultaneously functions as a heterogeneous oxidation catalyst and an optical reporter for reaction progress. During oxidation, the emission intensity at 440 nm increases with product formation and exhibits a strong quantitative correlation with benzaldehyde yield, enabling reaction progress to be continuously tracked across a series of substituted benzyl alcohols. Mechanistic studies indicate that the luminescence response is governed by competitive absorption and substrate-dependent interactions. Density functional theory calculations further reveal that benzyl alcohol forms stronger dispersion-stabilized π···π interactions with the emissive NDCA2– linkers than benzaldehyde, resulting in more pronounced luminescence quenching. As benzyl alcohol is converted into the more weakly interacting product, this quenching is progressively relieved, producing a measurable increase in emission intensity that reports the reaction progress. This integration provides a platform for reaction monitoring, process optimization, and future automated manufacturing.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
Luminescent Timeline
from Confined Active Radicals
Enables Infinite Cryptograph
content:
Abstract
The development of encryption materials is essential to meeting the increasing demand for information security. However, the present materials are susceptible to duplication due to a finite numbers of crypto states. Here, we report one chemical method to expand anticounterfeiting information from discrete, finite states to continuous, infinite states in the temporal domain by regulating the chemical reactions of luminescent radicals with the assistance of image-analysis technology. Infinite cryptographic materials were fabricated with continuous dynamic luminescence processes by integrating reversible radical reactions into confined radical luminescent systems. The inherent chemical kinetics of active radical emitters can be converted to time-dependent emission curves, serving as unclonable keys with nearly infinite crypto states in the temporal domain. Fluorescent AIE molecules were then introduced to expand the color gamut, further enriching the encoding capacity. These infinite cryptographic materials offer a robust anticounterfeiting platform, providing novel pathways for high-level information-protection applications.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
Protecting Groups as
Catalysts: Direct Synthesis of
Primary Amines from Ammonia under Carbonyl Catalysis
content:
Abstract
Primary amines are indispensable building blocks in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and functional materials, yet their direct, modular synthesis from ammonia remains challenging. Here we report a carbonyl catalysis strategy that enables the direct synthesis of structurally complex primary amines from ammonia by integrating the conventional multistep sequence of protection, N–H functionalization, and deprotection into a single catalytic cycle. As a proof of concept, amino-trifluoromethylation of alkenes using ammonium salts and Togni reagent afforded a wide range of β-trifluoromethylated primary amines, including derivatives of complex natural products. 1,8-Diazafluorenone was uniquely competent as a carbonyl catalyst, highlighting the critical role of catalyst design in ammonia transformation. Mechanistic studies suggest that its distinctive electronic structure facilitates the formation of the N–H ketimine intermediate, a prerequisite for catalytic turnover. These findings establish carbonyl catalysis as a platform for the direct transformation of ammonia and demonstrate how protecting groups can function as catalysts.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
Complementary
Acetonitrile Reduction and Amine Adsorption
on Mixed Cu–Ni Oxides for Electrocatalytic N-Ethylation
content:
Abstract
N-ethylamines are important motifs in pharmaceuticals and fine chemicals, but their selective synthesis from nitriles requires control over both nitrile reduction and amine availability at the catalyst-electrolyte interface. Herein, we investigate mixed Cu–Ni oxides for the aqueous electrocatalytic C–N coupling of acetonitrile (MeCN) with benzylamine (BA). The optimized Cu-NiO-0.5 catalyst affords N-ethylbenzylamine (EBA) in 75% yield with 87% selectivity and a mass-normalized formation rate of 12.5 mmol h–1 gcat–1 at −0.5 VRHE. Electrochemical testing indicates that the presence of CuO can promote the MeCN electrochemical reduction, generating abundant ethylimine for subsequent coupling. Meanwhile, the incorporation of Ni significantly enhances the adsorption of BA, accelerating the C–N coupling between the ethylimine and BA. In situ experimental measurements further confirm the sequential reduction-condensation-reduction pathway. Moreover, this strategy has also been proven to enable efficient C–N coupling between MeCN and various amine derivatives, giving the corresponding N-ethylated products in 58.3–84.6% yield and greater than 74% selectivity. This work offers an environmentally friendly strategy for the electrocatalytic synthesis of N-ethylamines.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
A Stable Phosphinidene
Radical Anion as a Multielectron
Reducing Agent
content:
Abstract
The diagonal relationship between carbon and phosphorus has long inspired comparisons between the chemistries of carbenes and phosphinidenes. However, while carbene chemistry has flourished over the past three decades, isolable phosphinidenes remain exceptionally rare, and their one-electron reduction products, phosphinidene radical anions, are unknown. Here, we report the synthesis and isolation of a crystalline phosphinidene radical anion through one-electron reduction of a ring-strained phosphanorcaradiene, a phosphinidene equivalent. Structural, spectroscopic, and computational studies reveal a monocoordinate phosphorus center where the unpaired electron is predominantly localized, in line with a highly reduced phosphorus center. The radical anion exhibits multielectron redox reactivity, including radical addition to an arylalkyne, sulfur atom transfer from isothiocyanate, elemental chalcogen activation, and stepwise oxidation to high-valent P(V) compounds through an overall five-electron process, integrating formal paramagnetic P(0)/P(II)/P(IV) radicals and diamagnetic P(I)/P(III)/P(V) derivatives.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
Cooperative Enantiomorphic-Site
and Chain-End Chirality
in Isoselective β-Lactone Polymerization
content:
Abstract
Polymer properties are profoundly impacted by tacticity, necessitating an understanding of the origins of stereocontrol to make high-performance materials. Recently, we reported that controlled incorporation of stereoerrors into trans-poly(3-hydroxy-2-methylbutyrate) (trans-PHMB) through the isoselective polymerization of rac-trans-3,4-dimethylpropiolactone (trans-DMPL) using racemic “sandwich” (BDI)Zn alkoxide complexes (where BDI = β-diketiminate) enables tuning of mechanical properties to match those of low-density polyethylene. However, the mechanism of stereocontrol of these catalysts was not explored. Herein, we report a thorough experimental and computational investigation uncovering a distinct manifestation of cooperative enantiomorphic-site and chain-end control, which we describe as site-mediated asymmetric chain-end control, where catalyst (Δ and Λ) and chain-end chiralities (R,R or S,S) work synergistically to influence the reaction’s stereoselectivity and rate. Experimental and computational data converge remarkably well, revealing that a Δ-catalyst with an (R,R)-chain end (Δ-RR) is isoselective 90% of the time. In contrast, a Δ-catalyst with an (S,S)-chain end (Δ-SS) is unselective. Detailed Density Functional Theory (DFT) investigations suggest molecular-level rationale for this mechanism of stereocontrol, demonstrating that chain positioning, monomer distortion, and ligand interactions work in conjunction to foster isoselectivity. Finally, DFT and kinetic modeling reveal that when polymerizing rac-trans-DMPL, the populations of Δ-RR and Δ-SS are equal and the high overall isoselectivity (mm% = 71–73%; where mm% is the percent of triads with a meso configuration across both ester linkages) of the catalyst is attributed to Δ-RR being faster than Δ-SS.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
Perfluoroalkyl Anion
Strategy to Construct Anion–π +  Type NIR-II
Phototheranostic Agents for Enhanced Tumor Immunotherapy
via Necroptosis/Ferroptosis
content:
Abstract
Anion-π+ photosensitizers (PSs) possess exceptional reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation and precise organelle targeting that could disrupt intracellular metabolic homeostasis and induce nonapoptotic cell death, offering unique advantages in overcoming immunosuppression. However, previous reports mainly focused on modifying the π+ core but often overlooked the crucial role of anions. Herein, we present a facile perfluoroalkyl anion strategy to modulate the fluorescence intensity and ROS generation capacity of anion-π+ PSs. Perfluorobutanesulfonate (PFB) anions with a single-sided perfluoroalkyl chain and bis(perfluorobutylsulfonyl)amide (BPFB) anions bearing double-sided perfluoroalkyl chains were employed to readily replace the hexafluoroantimonate (HFA) counterions in A/HFA and TPQ/HFA, yielding A/PFB, TPQ/PFB, A/BPFB, and TPQ/BPFB. Compared to the incorporated PFB anions, the BPFB anions more effectively restrict intramolecular motion through anion-π+ and van der Waals interactions, thereby significantly enhancing the fluorescence intensity of the phototheranostic agents─by 50.8-fold and 4.2-fold in A/BPFB nanoparticles (NPs) and TPQ/BPFB NPs compared to their HFA analogues, respectively. Concurrently, TPQ/BPFB NPs with second near-infrared emission demonstrated superior ROS generation, excellent mitochondrial targeting, and remarkable resistance to photobleaching. Strikingly, TPQ/BPFB NPs can activate both necroptosis and ferroptosis under irradiation, triggering a robust systemic immune response. Additionally, the lipophilicity granted by BPFB enables TPQ/BPFB NPs to infiltrate deeper into tumors, guaranteeing a more extensive photodynamic therapy with a 95% tumor suppression rate. Crucially, the immune memory triggered by TPQ/BPFB NPs effectively decreases the occurrence of lung metastases. Altogether, the perfluoroalkyl anion strategy proposed in this study offers new insights for developing potent anion-π+ PSs.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
MetallopeptiGELs: Injectable
Short-Peptide Supramolecular
Hydrogels Self-Assembled by Pd Nanosheets for Bioorthogonal Therapy
content:
Abstract
Controlling the delivery of chemotherapy to the tumor site is a long-standing goal of the medical field, as it could not only enhance the anticancer activity of the treatment but also reduce damage to the rest of the body. The emergence of bioorthogonal catalysis as a strategy capable of mediating continuous drug production in a nonenzymatic fashion has created the opportunity to develop so-called “bioorthogonal therapies,” which aim to generate the anticancer agents inside the tumors. Herein, we describe a novel class of supramolecular materials comprising ultrathin palladium nanosheets and fluorenylmethoxycarbonyl-diphenylalanine that self-assemble in water to form injectable, self-healing, biocompatible catalytic gels that convert inactive prodyes and prodrugs into active small molecules. The relatively weak physicochemical cross-links generated by the hybrid metal-peptide fibers facilitate the flow of the gel under mild shear stress (shear-thinning), thereby enabling precise intratumoral injections in vivo and localized prodrug activation. The strategy was validated in an aggressive pancreatic cancer xenograft model in mice, setting out a new direction for the field of bioorthogonal therapies.

title: The Battery Data Commons registry
content: Public battery datasets are growing rapidly, but fragmented hosting and inconsistent descriptions make them difficult to find, compare, and reuse. Battery Data Commons presently indexes 349 datasets in a living, searchable metadata registry, using human- and machine-readable descriptions linked to the original sources. This exposes experimental context without relocating raw data to give datasets wider visibility and a second life to legacy ones. Together, these capabilities provide infrastructure for reproducible battery science, engineering, and AI-enabled innovation.

title:
On Ammonia-Blended
Coke Oven Gas (COG) in Coaxial-Flow
Nonpremixed Flame for Decarbonization
content:
Abstract
Coke oven gas (COG) is a promising byproduct gas generated in steelmaking processes because of its high heating value and large production volume. The large amount of hydrogen in COG contributes to combustion reactivity, flame stability, and decarbonization. Recently, a strategy for recycling COG cofired with other fuels has been proposed to support continued utilization. Ammonia is an attractive carbon-free fuel, a suitable candidate for cofiring with COG. In this study, the combustion and emission characteristics of ammonia-blended COG were investigated using a coaxial-flow nonpremixed combustor. Experiments evaluated the flame length, blow-off limit, and OH radical and NOx emissions. 2D simulation using ANSYS Fluent analyzed flame temperature and NO mole fraction. As a result, it was found that the flame length decreased with increasing ammonia blending ratio because of the reduced heat release rate and fuel reactivity. The normalized correlation based on Roper’s equation accurately predicts the flame length of COG, implying that COG can subsequently be interpreted as a general-purpose fuel. In addition, despite decreased blow-off limit of the ammonia-blended COG, it still maintained a significantly higher stability limit than methane due to the high hydrogen content of COG. OH-PLIF measurements revealed that the flame structure and reaction intensity were only slightly affected by ammonia blending, demonstrating the feasibility of ammonia-blended COG for stable combustion. NOx emissions increased substantially because of enhanced fuel-NO formation. This study provides a fundamental database for ammonia-blended COG under nonpremixed conditions and can contribute to the development of low-carbon industrial combustion systems.

title:
Water-Locking and Its Release Effects in Argillaceous
Silt Hydrate-Bearing Sediments by NMR Technology
content:
Abstract
During natural gas hydrate production in the Shenhu area of the South China Sea, water released from hydrate dissociation coupled with formation water, may induce water-locking, which blocks gas flow pathways and restricts productivity. To elucidate the mechanisms and potential remediation strategies, this study employed low-field NMR to systematically investigate the spatiotemporal evolution of water-locking in argillaceous silt hydrate reservoirs at initial water saturations of 50%, 70%, 90%, and 100%, and evaluated three antiwaterblocking agents (fluorocarbon types I and II, and nonionic surfactant III). Results show that water-locking predominantly occurs in micropores (T2 < 10 ms, pore size < 1 μm), with intensity increasing exponentially with saturation through four stages (end-face, mid-end combined, wide-area, and full-domain water-locking) identifying 70% saturation as the critical range for the tested material. Agents I and II perform effectively at low to moderate saturations, but their efficacy is severely limited at saturations ≥90% and under fully saturated conditions. Displacement pressure synergistically enhances agent performance, yet pressure alone is insufficient. This study clarifies the evolution mechanisms and application boundaries of chemical remediation, offering theoretical guidance for water-locking prevention and efficient hydrate development in the South China Sea.

title:
Coupled Two-Phase Flow and Density-Driven Convective
Dissolution in a Deep Saline Aquifer during CO 2  Sequestration
content:
Abstract
The rise in greenhouse gas emissions has led to an increase in the Earth’s temperature. Carbon dioxide sequestration is chosen as a critical technology for reducing CO2 emissions into the atmosphere. Significant progress has already been made in CO2 sequestration, with numerous pilot projects and field-scale operations underway. The trapping mechanisms involved in deep saline aquifers help in long-term storage. However, the studies on the coupled effects of flow and various trapping mechanisms are limited. Therefore, in the current work, the coupled two-phase flow and density-driven convective dissolution were studied using numerical simulations in COMSOL Multiphysics. The model is assumed to be isothermal and homogeneous. The primary results showed that pressure and saturation changes during injection and after shutdown have a significant impact on convective dissolution, which differs from single-phase models. In the mathematical framework, a solubility model is implemented to understand the effect of equilibrium concentration on convective dissolution quantitatively, followed by a sensitivity analysis conducted by varying the composition of brine, permeability, and Rayleigh number. From the brine composition sensitivity study, brine density, viscosity, and equilibrium concentration variation with brine composition were identified as crucial for convective dissolution as well as CO2 plume migration. Later, permeability variation showed that convective dissolution accelerated with an increase in permeability. Then, the combination of fluid and rock properties used in the Rayleigh number investigation showed a significant impact on saturation and pressure changes in the aquifer. Hence, the integration of two-phase flow dynamics is found to be pivotal for characterizing the convective dissolution trapping in a deep saline aquifer.

title:
A Review
on Isotopic Traceability of Renewable Oils
in Co-Processed Fuels: Exploring the Analytical Potential of IRMS
content:
Abstract
Reducing dependence on fossil fuels through the integration of renewable oils into the refinery infrastructure requires an accurate determination of the renewable fraction in the final products, which remains challenging in complex matrices where fossil and biogenic feedstocks exhibit similar isotopic signatures. Accelerator mass spectrometry (AMS) is the current reference method, but its high cost, limited accessibility, and long analysis time motivate the search for alternatives. This review examines the application of isotope ratio mass spectrometry (IRMS) for tracing renewable content in coprocessed systems, discussing its capabilities and limitations based on studies that demonstrate its feasibility at low blend ratios with characterized end-members, system-specific calibration, and validation against AMS, which may support refineries in optimizing biogenic carbon introduction through accessible, fast, and low-cost equipment. Remaining challenges include the limited number of investigations available, the isotopic contrast between renewable and fossil end-members, the lack of standardized methodologies and validation protocols for routine analysis, and the predominant reliance on a stable carbon isotope signature. Other approaches for renewable fraction determination, including energy and mass balance methods, were also discussed together with current challenges and future perspectives for IRMS development. Whereas previous reviews broadly compare renewable carbon tracking methods for coprocessed fuels, this review focuses specifically on the analytical potential, current evidence base, and unresolved limitations of IRMS for renewable carbon traceability.

title:
Fundamental Determination of the Average Relative
Molecular Mass of Distillate Fuels Using the Ideal Gas Law
content:
Abstract
The average relative molecular mass is an indicator of properties relevant to the evaluation and regulation of transportation fuels. An accurate and repeatable method of measurement is therefore crucial. Current techniques, such as through size-exclusion chromatography, gas chromatography–mass spectrometry, and vapor pressure osmometry, involve complex measurement systems which necessitate calibration and/or correlating functions. This paper describes and validates a new method using the ideal gas law, providing a simpler measurement system with lower uncertainty. At constant volume and temperature, the pressure of a gas is directly proportional to the number of moles of it present, which is equal to its mass divided by its molecular mass. It follows that an independently measured mass of hydrocarbon mixture can be vaporized when introduced into a chamber of constant volume at a sufficient and constant temperature. A pressure change inside the chamber can be measured with which the number of moles present, and consequently, the average relative molecular mass of the mixture can be determined through the ideal gas law. The accuracy of this method depends on the homogeneity of the conditions and the applicability of the ideal gas law. The method was validated by using it to determine the average relative molecular mass of pure hydrocarbons and known mixtures up to a molecular mass of 130 g mol–1. The average relative molecular mass of six FACE gasolines (Fuels for Advanced Combustion Engines) and Haltermann E10 certification fuel is measured to below 5% uncertainty and compared to determinations by detailed hydrocarbon analysis (DHA) and five empirical correlations.

title:
Coupling Mechanisms of Wax Precipitation and Wellbore
Deposition Prediction in HTHP Condensate Gas Wells
content:
Abstract
Wax precipitation and wellbore deposition commonly occur during the development of high-temperature and high-pressure condensate gas wells, posing significant challenges to flow assurance and production stability. In this study, a high-temperature and high-pressure dynamic wax precipitation apparatus was employed to determine the wax appearance temperature under flowing conditions based on abrupt changes in pressure difference. The effects of pressure, gas–oil ratio (GOR), flow rate, injection gas medium, and wax content on wax precipitation in condensate oil–gas systems were systematically investigated, and a gas–liquid–solid three-phase wax precipitation phase behavior model was established. The results show that the wax appearance temperature is jointly controlled by liquid-phase wax supersaturation, gas–liquid compositional partitioning, and deposition kinetics. Under high-pressure dynamic conditions at 50 MPa, an increase in wax content by 7.40 percentage points, from 26.56% to 33.96%, increased the wax appearance temperature by 8.7 °C. The pressure effect exhibits a nonmonotonic, dew-point-controlled segmented pattern: as pressure increases from 10 to 57.8 MPa, the wax appearance temperature rises from 26.6 to 34.0 °C, whereas it decreases to 32.9 °C when pressure further increases to 77.8 MPa. When the GOR increases from 850 m3/m3 to 1600 m3/m3, the wax appearance temperature decreases from 30.4 to 23.8 °C. Among the different injection gases, the wax appearance temperature follows the order N2 > produced gas > CO2. Flow rate has only a weak effect on wax appearance temperature and mainly regulates wax deposition intensity. The proposed phase-behavior model reasonably captures the turning behavior of wax appearance temperature near the dew-point pressure and enables wax deposition risk prediction when coupled with wellbore pressure–temperature profiles. These findings provide mechanistic insights into wax precipitation and deposition in high-temperature and high-pressure condensate gas wells and offer a theoretical basis for optimizing wax control strategies.

title:
Depth-Dependent
CO 2  Storage Efficiency:
A Numerical Simulation Study of Saline Aquifers
content:
Abstract
Estimation of CO2 storage efficiency with depth is important for assessing the feasibility, scalability, and long-term performance of carbon capture and storage (CCS) projects. Previous studies have reported inconsistent observations regarding the variation of storage efficiency with depth, including a nonlinear trend in which structural storage efficiency declines to zero near 2400 m, nonzero simulated storage efficiencies by the DOE-NETL, and claims of completely leak-free storage at greater depths due to phase-density reversal. A consistent and validated understanding of depth-dependent storage efficiency based on exhaustive reservoir fluid dynamics and reactive phase equilibrium is unavailable. This study presents a comprehensive numerical investigation of CO2 storage efficiency in saline aquifers as a function of depth using 2-D CMG-GEM simulations conducted over 1000 years, with all key flow dynamics and thermodynamic parameters defined as depth-dependent. Results show that total CO2 storage efficiency decreases from ∼0.92 at 800 m and 0.99 at 1200 m to ∼0.76 at 2500 m and remains within a narrow band at greater depths. Total CO2 leakage efficiency increases from ∼0.02 at 800 m to a maximum of ∼0.35 at 4000 m, and then declines to ∼0.22 at 11,000 m. The CO2 storage capacity per unit pore volume increases continuously with depth, reaching ∼980 kg/m3 at approximately 11,000 m, with ∼860 kg/m3 stored in the aqueous phase, ∼20 kg/m3 as supercritical CO2, and ∼100 kg/m3 in mineral form. Beyond ∼11,000 m depth, distinct liquid and gas phases disappear under supercritical pressure and temperature conditions, indicating the absence of density reversal within the 800–12,000 m range modeled here and nonzero leakage of CO2 in the supercritical water–CO2 mixture. Sensitivity analyses further show that the overall trends in storage and leakage efficiency are only weakly affected by reservoir heterogeneity, anisotropy, grid size, and variations in flow dynamics parameters.

title: Three-Dimensionally Fibrillated Inorganic Composite Anion Exchange Membranes for Ampere-Scale Hydrogen Production
content:
Abstract
Hydroxide-induced degradation and swelling of organic anion exchange membranes (AEMs) fundamentally limit the advancement and industrialization of alkaline hydrogen production. Here, we present a free-standing inorganic AEM comprising 90 wt % layered double hydroxides within a three-dimensionally fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene scaffold. The membrane achieves zero swelling, suppressed hydrogen crossover, and a low area-specific resistance of 0.089 Ω cm2 while remaining stable for 1344 h in 1 M and 30 wt % KOH at 80 °C, under which commercial polymeric membranes fail rapidly. The confined hydrogen-bond network within layer double hydroxide galleries promotes Grotthuss-dominated OH– transport as supported by ab initio molecular dynamics. The membrane sustains 1 A cm–2 operation for 550 h in AEM water electrolyzers and 425 h in alkaline water electrolyzers, establishing a durable inorganic AEM platform for alkaline hydrogen production and related electrochemical energy technologies.

title: Low-Cost Iron/Manganese-Based Polyanionic Cathodes for Sustainable Na-Ion Batteries
content:
Abstract
Sustainable Na-ion batteries (NIBs) have attracted widespread attention in transportation vehicles and large-scale energy storage systems due to abundant sodium sources, high safety records, and favorable all-climate performance. However, their overall performance and cost are largely governed by cathode materials, which determine practical application and commercial market prospects. Iron- and/or manganese-based polyanionic cathodes not only reduce cost but also provide high working voltage and desirable cycling stability, benefiting from strong inductive effects and robust structural covalency of polyanionic groups, making them attractive for sustainable batteries. This review summarizes material design concepts, research progress, technological bottlenecks, and development directions for various types of phosphate, pyrophosphate, and sulfate cathodes. Besides, we focus on clarifying the structure–function relationships by comprehensively comparing synthesis methods, crystal structures, electrochemical behavior, and reaction mechanisms of Fe/Mn-based polyanionic cathodes for NIBs. This review provides critical guidance for the future advancement of practical NIBs.

title: Disentangling Static and Dynamic Contributions to the Urbach Energy in Mixed Sn–Pb Perovskites
content:
Abstract
Sn–Pb perovskites are promising low-bandgap absorbers for photovoltaics, but their efficiency is limited by the low open-circuit voltage, VOC. The VOC deficit, WOC, is related to energetic disorder, characterized by the Urbach energy, EU, comprising static and dynamic contributions. For Cs0.25FA0.75SnxPb1–xI3, these contributions were determined using time-resolved microwave conductivity (TRMC) and photoluminescence (PL) measurements between 180–350 K. For Pb-based films, both techniques provided similar EU values. However, for Sn-containing compositions (x = 0.2 and 0.5), TRMC-derived EU were twice higher than those found by PL. These differences arise from compositional heterogeneity: TRMC integrates absorption over the entire thickness while the PL-derived absorption originates from low-bandgap domains, likely from the Sn-rich top surface as revealed by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). The PL-derived EU trend corresponds to the bandgap-normalized WOC, which is smallest for x = 0.5 (∼9.2 meV), attributed to the low dynamic contribution originating from the lower mass of Sn.

title: Insoluble π –d -Conjugated Small Molecules Featuring  p -Type Ligands Enable All-Organic Dual-Ion Batteries
content:
Abstract
Organic electrodes for secondary batteries are hindered by molecular dissolution and low operating voltages. Herein, we report a coordination-driven strategy to construct insoluble π–d conjugated small molecules (BTD-M, M = Cu, Ni, or Zn) featuring high-voltage p-type triphenylamine-derived ligands (N4′,N4′-diphenyl-[1,1′-biphenyl]-3,4,4′-triamine, BTD). By precisely tuning metal–ligand coordination, we thermodynamically lock discrete molecules against electrolyte dissolution while preserving unhindered access to active sites. The optimal BTD-Cu exhibits a narrow bandgap of 0.7 eV, enabling extensive electron delocalization for electronic conductivity. This electrode delivers a near-theoretical capacity of 134 mAh g–1 at 1C and still delivers 83 mAh g–1 at 10C. Leveraging bipolar redox chemistry of p-type ligands and metal centers, the symmetric all-organic dual-ion battery achieves an average voltage of 2.4 V and a cycle life exceeding 1000 cycles. This work establishes insoluble π–d conjugated small molecules as an accessible platform for organic battery design.

title: Weakly Coordinating Polyester Enables High Performance Semi-solid Polymer Electrolyte for Li–Metal Batteries
content:
Abstract
Lithium metal batteries leveraging semi-solid polymer electrolytes (SSPEs) promise to increase the energy density of Li-ion batteries. These polymer–plasticizer hybrids offer mechanical robustness, yet their performance is often limited by preferential Li+ coordination to solvating polymer matrices. Here, we demonstrate that replacing a conventional polyether with a weakly coordinating polyester, i.e., poly(caprolactone) diacrylate, mitigates this effect and fundamentally alters Li+ transport and interfacial behavior. The SSPE delivers stable cycling with 80% capacity retention after 188 cycles in full cells employing an NMC622 cathode with a 2 mA h cm–2 loading and a 25 µm Li–metal anode (N/P = 2.5).

title: Synergistic Side-Chain Design of Poly(aryl Quinuclidinium) Anion Exchange Membranes for Fuel Cells
content:
Abstract
Anion exchange membrane fuel cells (AEMFCs) offer a route to hydrogen-to-energy conversion. However, the lack of anion-exchange-membranes (AEMs) with desirable performance severely hampers their commercialization. Herein, we design conductive and alkaline-stable AEMs based on poly(aryl quinuclidinium) with two types of side chains, namely fluorine-terminated alkyl chains and quinuclidinium-capped alkyl chains suitable for AEMFC setup. The side chains induce well-formed microphase separation structures and increase free volume, while the stable quinuclidinium cations on the backbone and side chain prevent nucleophilic substitution and Hofmann elimination under high-temperature harsh alkaline conditions. The optimized AEMs combine an ion conductivity of 185.06 mS cm–1 at 80 °C, tensile strength of 55.24 MPa, elongation at break of 11.22%, and retention of essentially all of their ionic conductivity after 1800 h of immersion in 10 M NaOH at 80 °C. The fuel cell incorporating the optimized membrane (QPPTQ-Qui-BF) demonstrates a peak power density of 1432 mW cm–2 at a current density of 2334 mA cm–2 and a cell voltage of 0.614 V at 80 °C. These results indicate that side-chain engineering of poly(aryl quinuclidinium) backbones is an effective route to AEMs for energy conversion devices.

title: Electrochemical Pathway to Large Flake Ti 3 C 2 T  x   MXenes via Controlled Aluminum Dissolution for High Performance Supercapacitors
content:
Abstract
Conventional MXene synthesis relies on hazardous concentrated HF, raising safety, and environmental concerns despite the outstanding electrical and mechanical properties of the resulting MXenes. Here, we demonstrate an electrochemical etching protocol using a carbon cloth working electrode and HBF4/water electrolyte to selectively remove Al from Ti3AlC2 MAX phase. Applying a constant potential of 1 V drives anodic Al dissolution via a controlled redox process, minimizing HF generation while preserving the Ti-C backbone. The resulting Ti3C2Tx nanosheets exhibit substantially larger flake sizes compared to conventionally etched MXene, while retaining their hexagonal structure. Structural, vibrational, chemical, and morphological evidence confirms that Al is selectively etched under electrochemical bias. Furthermore, the electrochemically synthesized Ti3C2Tx was employed as an electrode material for electrochemical energy storage applications. The electrochemically etched MXene (EDM-1V) exhibits a high areal capacitance of ∼164 mF cm–2 at a scan rate of 10 mV s–1 and promising cycling stability, outperforming both electrochemically etched at 0 V (EDM-0V) and conventionally HF etched MXene (HF-DM). This work provides a safe, scalable, and mechanistically guided electrochemical route that positions Ti3C2Tx as a promising candidate for energy storage technologies.

title: Synthesis of Zr-Doped BaTaO 2 N Platelets from a TaC Precursor for Efficient Photocatalytic H 2  Production
content:
Abstract
Two-dimensional (2D) perovskite-type oxynitrides are highly attractive for photocatalytic solar-to-chemical conversion, yet conventional molten-salt synthesis is severely challenged by sensitive binary flux controls and dense structural defects. Herein, we developed a streamlined, single-component potassium chloride (KCl) molten-salt-assisted thermal nitridation strategy utilizing an innovative tantalum carbide (TaC) and barium hydroxide (Ba(OH)2) precursor combination to direct the growth of well-defined, single-crystalline 2D barium tantalum oxynitride (BaTaO2N) platelets. Concurrently, atomistic Zr4+ substitution efficiently alleviates detrimental Ta3+ defects and elevates the conduction band potential to amplify the thermodynamic driving force for proton reduction. When decorated with platinum@chromium oxide (Pt@Cr2O3) core–shell structured cocatalysts, the optimized Zr-doped BaTaO2N platelets register a maximum initial average H2 evolution rate of 305 μmol h–1 and an apparent quantum yield (AQY) of about 3.24% at 450 nm under mild sacrificial conditions. Furthermore, femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy verifies that this continuous core–shell architecture delivers the highest sub-nanosecond electron extraction efficiency among all configurations. Overall, this work provides a robust synthesis strategy for preparing highly crystalline 2D Ta-based oxynitride platelets and optimizes their interfacial carrier management for efficient solar hydrogen production.

title: Liquid Phase Backscattered Scanning Electron Microscopy of Bacillus subtilis Spores
content:
Graphene encapsulation enables liquid‐phase BSE‐SEM to visualize subsurface architecture of whole, hydrated Bacillus subtilis spores without staining. This approach is applied to visualize dormant spores and subsequent structural changes during spore germination, while imaging across a range of beam energies and Monte Carlo simulations provide a framework for understanding depth‐sensitive contrast in thick, hydrated biological specimens.








ABSTRACT
Backscattered electron scanning electron microscopy (BSE‐SEM) provides compositional image contrast but has found limited application to biological samples due to the low atomic number difference between constituent elements, the thickness of the surrounding environment, and the need for complex sample preparation. Previous graphene‐encapsulation SEM studies have demonstrated imaging of hydrated bacteria, principally to preserve or observe bacterial morphology. Here, we establish liquid phase BSE‐SEM (LPBSEM) as a depth‐sensitive, label‐free approach for visualizing subsurface architecture in intact hydrated bacteria and Bacillus subtilis spores. This approach does not require staining and enables high‐contrast visualization of subcellular structures in hydrated samples. Internal structural layers within B. subtilis spores have been observed similar to those visualized with conventional thin‐section transmission electron microscopy but without the need for sample preparation that potentially compromises sample integrity. We further investigate the influence of beam energy on the interaction volume depth and image contrast and propose optimal conditions for subsurface visualization. Monte Carlo simulations were used to assess whether the observed contrast trends are consistent with expected backscatter distributions and provide a physical framework for interpretation and understanding of BSE generation from hydrated, low atomic number specimens.

title: Operando Electro‐Rheology: Unraveling Decoupled Ion Transport‐Mechanical‐Morphological Properties in Nanostructured Block Copolymer Electrolytes
content:
A novel operando methodology, which combines simultaneous rheological and electrochemical measurements under dc polarization in a LiTFSI‐doped polystyrene‐block‐poly(ethylene oxide) block copolymer electrolyte, is developed. Time‐resolved monitoring of the viscoelastic and electrochemical responses to galvanostatic stimulus enables to elucidate the coupled behavior of the block copolymer electrolyte, providing simultaneous insight into ion transport, mechanical response, and morphological evolution.








ABSTRACT
Block copolymer electrolytes exhibit a complex interplay between self‐assembled morphology, ion transport, and mechanical properties under galvanostatic battery cycling. Here, we propose a novel operando methodology combining concurrent rheology and electrochemical measurements upon dc polarization for a lithium bis (trifluoromethanesulfonyl) imide (LiTFSI) doped polystyrene‐block‐poly (ethylene oxide) diblock copolymer electrolyte. Time‐resolved measurements of the viscoelastic and electrochemical responses to the galvanostatic stimulus permit to uncover the effective response of the block copolymer electrolyte, tracking ion transport‐mechanical‐morphological properties simultaneously. Corroborated by scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) imaging, we observe the block copolymer transitioning from unperturbed, increasingly aligned lamellae to reorganized self‐assembled nanostructures as the applied current density approaches the limiting current and, beyond its onset, the nanomorphology evolves toward gyroid and hexagonal phases. The diffusion coefficients decrease as current density increases, which is attributed to concentration polarization phenomena. Lastly, this methodology identifies a direct coupling between interfacial electrochemical processes and mechanical properties, highlighting the intimate interplay between interfacial phenomena and rubbery plateau modulus upon current densities.

title: Atomically Dispersed Fe–Mo Catalytic Pairs Enable Two‐Electron Li2C2O4 Pathway for Reversible Li–CO2 Batteries
content:
Electronically asymmetric Fe1‐Mo1 dual‐atom catalytic pairs anchored on CN construct a donor‐acceptor bridge that enables dynamic charge redistribution and Fe–N–Mo redox coupling, synergistically regulating CO2 activation and oxalate decomposition, thus driving a reversible two‐electron Li2C2O4‐dominated pathway for high‐performance Li–CO2 battery.








ABSTRACT
Lithium‐carbon dioxide (Li–CO2) batteries present a promising strategy for coupling high‐energy storage with CO2 utilization, yet their development is impeded by sluggish kinetics and severe polarization associated with insulating discharge products. Achieving selective and reversible two‐electron conversion toward Li2C2O4 remains a critical challenge for improving energy efficiency and cycling stability. Herein, we report electronically asymmetric dual‐atom Fe–N–Mo catalytic pairs anchored on a highly conjugated N‐doped carbon (NC) framework, forming Fe1‐Mo1 integrated catalytic pairs (Fe1‐Mo1/ICPs) to promote a reversible two‐electron Li2C2O4 conversion pathway. The πconjugated highly conjugated N‐doped carbon framework stabilizes atomically dispersed Fe and Mo sites while enhancing inter‐site electronic coupling. Within the proposed heteronuclear Fe–N–Mo configuration, intrinsic electronic asymmetry generates electrophilic Fe and nucleophilic Mo sites, enabling dynamic charge redistribution and complementary catalytic behavior. Such a donor‐acceptor bridge effectively regulates intermediate adsorption/desorption and suppresses competing reaction pathways, thereby favoring the selective and reversible formation of Li2C2O4. Operando spectroscopic analysis confirms the preferential reversible Li2C2O4 evolution during cycle, while density functional theory calculations reveal substantially reduced energy barriers for key reaction intermediates. Benefiting from the unique electronic environment and synergistic effects of asymmetric dual‐atom sites, the FeMoCN catalyst delivers outstanding electrochemical performance.

title: Charge‐State‐Controlled Surface Modifiers for High‐Voltage and Stable Wide‐Bandgap Perovskite Solar Cells
content:
A charge‐neutralized organic ion‐paired surface modifier strategy is demonstrated to overcome the operational instability of wide‐bandgap perovskite photovoltaics. This molecular configuration retains a stable low‐dimensional surface phase under operational stress. Consequently, the resulting interface obstructs defect‐mediated ion migration pathways, suppressing halide segregation to deliver a high open‐circuit voltage of 1.326 V in 1.77 eV perovskite solar cells.








ABSTRACT
For wide‐bandgap mixed‐halide perovskites, quasi‐two‐dimensional (quasi‐2D) surface reconstruction using bulky‐cation spacers is widely employed to passivate surface defects and disrupt halide migration pathways. Nevertheless, under operational stress, conventional ammonium‐based spacers can undergo deprotonation, destabilizing the low‐dimensional surface layer and weakening its function. Herein, we report an organic‐spacer charge‐state control strategy for the surface modification of Cs0.2FA0.8PbI1.8Br1.2 wide‐bandgap perovskites. This strategy involves combining octylammonium (OA) with N‐methylsulfanilic acid (NMSA) to form NMSAO, a charge‐neutralized ammonium–sulfonate modifier state. This configuration induces an associated Ruddlesden–Popper‐like quasi‐2D phase at the perovskite surface that suppresses trap‐mediated recombination, facilitates interfacial charge extraction, and disrupts halide‐ion migration pathways. As a result, the NMSAO‐treated perovskite solar cells (PSCs) achieved a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 19.83% and an open‐circuit voltage (VOC) of 1.326 V, compared with 17.30% and 1.197 V for the untreated control PSCs. Furthermore, the NMSAO‐treated PSCs retain 93.59% of their initial PCE after 500 h of continuous illumination under ISOS‐L‐1 conditions and more than 93% after 500 h of thermal aging at 85°C. This study demonstrates the effectiveness of a charge‐neutralized organic spacer for quasi‐2D surface reconstruction in wide‐bandgap mixed‐halide PSCs, improving both photovoltaic performance and operational stability.

title:
Biphasic Polyarylisocyanide
Liquid Crystals with Enhanced
Enantiodiscrimination for Residual Chemical Shift Anisotropy Measurements
content:
Abstract
Anisotropic NMR spectroscopy has emerged as a powerful tool for the structural elucidation of complex small molecules. Compared with residual dipolar couplings (RDCs), however, the application of residual chemical shift anisotropies (RCSAs) has remained relatively limited, largely owing to the lack of simple and efficient methods for their acquisition. Here, we report a biphasic polyarylisocyanide lyotropic liquid-crystalline (LLC) system based on single-handed helical polyisocyanides prepared by alkyne-Pd(II)-catalyzed controlled polymerization. The biphasic nature of this medium enables straightforward extraction of ΔRCSAs from a single one-dimensional 13C NMR experiment on a single sample, without requiring specialized instrumentation, devices, or postcorrection. We demonstrate the broad applicability of this approach by measuring ΔRCSAs for eight structurally diverse natural products and organic molecules. The resulting 13C ΔRCSAs are sufficiently large to enable reliable structural verification and stereochemical elucidation. Notably, the method allowed us to unambiguously resolve previously questionable 13C NMR assignments in cryptotanshinone. In addition, the chiral LLC medium exhibits pronounced enantiodiscrimination, as demonstrated for indanol enantiomers as well as significant enantiodifferentiating capabilities for several natural alkaloids. Furthermore, 19F RCSA measurements enable direct differentiation of two enantiomers even within a racemic mixture. Together, these results establish biphasic polyarylisocyanide LLCs as a simple, robust, and broadly applicable alignment platform for ΔRCSA measurements, thereby expanding the utility of anisotropic NMR for structural elucidation and chiral molecular characterization.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
Solid–Liquid
Transitions in 1D Metal–Organic
Chalcogenolates
content:
Abstract
A lack of melt processability is noted for emerging hybrid material systems like metal–organic frameworks, lead-halide perovskites, and metal–organic chalcogenolates (MOChas). Here, we report reversible solid-to-liquid phase transitions ranging from 67 to 184 °C in silver secondary-alkanethiolate 1-dimensional (1D) MOChas. These MOChas were synthesized using five different secondary alkanethiols: 2-propanethiol, 2-butanethiol, 2-pentanethiol, 3-hexanethiol, and 4-heptanethiol. Structural characterization using small-molecule serial femtosecond crystallography (smSFX) reveals a 1D wire crystal motif. These 1D wire lattices exhibit green-yellow photoluminescence that disappears upon melting. The low melting temperature is attributed to the conformational flexibility of the secondary alkanethiol ligands, providing entropic benefits for the amorphous state. Furthermore, the transition from a nonmolecular, infinite covalent (Ag-SR)∞ network in the solid state to oligomolecular species (Ag-SR)x in the molten state contributes to a higher enthalpy of fusion. Large crystallites are observed to evolve from the liquid near the phase transition temperature. Notably, unmixing of chiral domains occurs in the racemic crystals while the inorganic network remains unchanged.

title:
Solid-State NMR Reveals
a Bifunctional Disordered
Linker That Couples Katanin Microtubule Anchoring to Condensate-Activated
Severing
content:
Abstract
Microtubule severing by katanin drives rapid cytoskeletal remodeling for cell fate decision, yet how the catalytic subunit p60 (Kp60) recognizes the microtubule lattice to achieve efficient severing remains unresolved. Here, we report that the N-terminal intrinsically disordered region (IDR) of Kp60 is an essential bifunctional module for severing activity. Using solid-state NMR (ssNMR), we identified a microtubule-binding domain (MTBD) within the IDR which directly engages the lattice to guide substrate anchoring. Surprisingly, the same IDR also enables Kp60 phase separation. Our ssNMR analyses of the condensed phase pinpointed three discrete interaction regions within the IDR which cooperatively orchestrate this multivalent assembly. Importantly, Kp60 phase separation was associated with markedly increased ATPase activity, supporting a functional link between condensation and enzymatic activation. Using function-separation-mutation analyses, our studies show both microtubule binding and condensation are essential for severing: microtubule targeting provides spatial specificity, while condensation provides the catalytic threshold through local enrichment. Thus, the Kp60 IDR constitutes a bifunctional interface that integrates substrate recognition with enzymatic robustness, thereby establishing phase separation as a fundamental and efficient regulator of microtubule dynamics and cytoskeletal remodeling.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
C–C
Bond Formation via the Addition or Redistribution
of Hydrogen: Chemical Synthesis Beyond Premetalated Reagents or Metallic
Reductants
content:
Abstract
Stoichiometric organometallic reagents are used in countless C–C bond-forming processes but are often hazardous, display poor functional group compatibility, and require multistep preparation from the parent platform chemicals. Zerovalent metals are also used to mediate reductive C–C bond formation, but their use at scale poses similar safety and engineering concerns. The formation of C-nucleophiles as transient catalytic intermediates via hydrogen transfer from abundant low-molecular-weight reductants (H2, Me2CHOH, HCO2H) offers a more ideal alternative to preformed carbanions or zerovalent metals in reductive C–C bond formation. Related hydrogen autotransfer processes where reactants serve as redox pairs en route to products of C–C coupling also are desirable, as they avoid both sacrificial reductants and premetalated reagents. In this Review, hydrogen-mediated variants of classical reactions that exploit carbanions or zerovalent metals are described.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
Breaking Symmetry Cancellation:
Heterovalent Substitution
Unlocks Ultrastrong, Phase-Matchable Nonlinearity in Deep-Ultraviolet
Tetrahedral Crystals
content:
Abstract
Deep-ultraviolet (deep-UV) nonlinear optical (NLO) crystals demand a challenging integration of strong second-harmonic generation (SHG), sufficient birefringence for phase matching (PM), and a wide bandgap (λ < 200 nm). In tetrahedron-based materials, the hyperpolarizabilities of constituent tetrahedra usually nearly cancel due to structural symmetry, resulting in weak SHG and small birefringence─a classic example being α-SiO2. Breaking this symmetry-driven cancellation while retaining deep-UV transparency thus represents a key chemical design challenge. Here, we report a deep-UV transparent NLO crystal BeSO4 derived from α-SiO2 via stepwise heterovalent tetrahedral substitution. This crystal crystallizes in the noncentrosymmetric tetragonal space group, with alternating BeO4 and SO4 tetrahedra forming [Be3S3O18] six-membered rings. By effectively breaking the symmetry cancellation via alternating low-valence (Be2+) and high-valence (S6+) tetrahedra, BeSO4 achieves a deep-UV cutoff at 176 nm, an exceptional SHG response of 5.1 × KDP at 1064 nm─the strongest among all deep-UV sulfates and Be-containing deep-UV crystals, and a birefringence of 0.038 at 590 nm, almost seven times that of the isostructural BPO4. Unlike BPO4 and α-SiO2, BeSO4 exhibits SHG behavior consistent with phase-matchability, and under 532 nm excitation, it produces a detectable second-harmonic signal at 266 nm. First-principles calculations reveal that the enhanced performance originates from shorter S–O bonds, stronger orbital hybridization, a narrower bandgap, and highly anisotropic electron density, all stemming from the successful cancellation-breaking strategy. It should be noted that the main novelty of this work lies in single-crystal growth, linear/nonlinear optical properties, and mechanistic analysis, since the crystal structure of BeSO4 has been previously reported.
